# EU Cowork AI

> Open-source AI work platform for companies. Access to more than 100 language models, processed in the EU. Self-hostable from a single user under the MIT licence, or operated in ISO 27001 certified data centres in Switzerland. An offering of Herr Informatik GmbH, Windisch, Switzerland.

Last updated: 2026-09-05.

Built for use across the company.
EU Cowork AI connects your systems, carries out work under controlled access, and stays accountable to your IT at all times.
Connect your systems
Connect ERP, SharePoint, company knowledge and further tools centrally to EU Cowork AI. Native connectors are available right away, your own systems you attach through MCP or a REST API.
Control access centrally
Decide by role, group or user who may reach which systems and functions. Access to invoices can be allowed, for example, while sensitive payroll data stays blocked.
Get real work done
EU Cowork AI does more than answer questions: it creates files, evaluates ERP data and takes over recurring tasks. Finished Excel, Word or PDF documents are ready right in the chat.
Account for everything
Every tool call, every admin action and every login is logged continuously. Your IT can see at any time who accessed which data, and export the entries.
Fit into existing work
Use your AI coworker where your team already works. In the chat, right next to an open Outlook email and, in future, in further applications: support without constant switching and copying.
OIDC and Entra ID Sign in through your existing directory. Groups and roles come along with it.
Pooled budgets One monthly budget for the organisation instead of per-head limits, with a soft block instead of silent overage.

Source code coming soon Install it on your own server
Clone the repository
One clone, every service. An ordinary Docker Compose stack, nothing exotic.
$ git clone https://github.com/Herr-Informatik-org/eu-cowork.git
Copy
The clone works as soon as the GitHub repository is published under the MIT license, which is coming soon. Until then, the full installation guide with system requirements and measured figures is available in the documentation .
Install and start
The installer generates the secrets, pulls the images and starts the stack with automatic TLS. On a fresh Ubuntu server, setup-server.sh prepares the machine first.
$ cd eu-cowork/distribution && ./install.sh
Copy
Installation, stack and system requirements
Built on LibreChat A thin fork of LibreChat, over 40,000 stars on GitHub and in use worldwide.
No seat limit No price per head, no forced branding, no feature behind an enterprise gate.
Open formats, your database A standard Docker stack with MongoDB and open file formats. If you leave, you take everything with you.
From a single person One command, one server. For one person too, and free for good.
Frequently asked.
Where is my data processed? +
Operated in Switzerland (Green Lupfig), inference EU-processed via EuRouter. Self-hosted, data stays entirely on your infrastructure.
Is my data used for training? +
No. No-training, telemetry off by default.
Is this really open source? +
The GitHub repository under the MIT license is coming soon: the source is not public yet, we are hardening it first. After that: self-hosting free from 1 user, no seat limit, no forced branding. The base it builds on, LibreChat, is MIT today.
Which models are available? +
Over 100 models via EuRouter, including the large models from Anthropic and OpenAI.
Can I connect my ERP? +
Yes, via the MCP gateway with granular RBAC and per-call audit.
Is there an app? +
Today an installable PWA; native iOS/Android app planned.
Is EU Cowork AI available inside Outlook? +
Yes, as an add-in in beta: a pane next to the open email that summarises, drafts replies, translates and pulls out tasks. In internal use at our place today, not yet generally available.

Frequently asked questions
What does self-hosting cost?
Nothing for the software itself. Costs arise outside of it: the server the stack runs on, and the model usage you settle directly with your provider. At idle, the base stack uses around 0.7 GB of memory, and a shared VM carries several instances. The measured figures and the sizing guidance are documented under Self-hosting .
What is included in managed operation?
A dedicated instance in an ISO 27001-certified data centre in Switzerland, plus operations, updates, backups and monitoring. It also includes a monthly model credit available to the entire organisation as a shared pool rather than capped per head. Once it is used up, access is blocked rather than quietly billed on.
Is the feature set identical?
Yes, entirely. There is no second edition with additional features, no seat limit and no forced branding. Permission management down to tool level, audit log, central budgets and enterprise login are part of the scope in both operating models. What that means in detail is documented under Governance .
Can I switch between the operating models later?
Yes, in both directions. Both paths use the same architecture, so switching is a migration rather than a new rollout: conversations, accounts, settings and uploads come along. The procedure is documented under Backup and migration .
Which operating model suits your company?
Request managed operation View self-hosting

Frequently asked questions.
What prospective customers ask us before signing up, and what we answer.
Open all answers
How signing up works
Does the product already exist, or is this just a page with a form? +
The platform is ready for production use and in internal use at Herr Informatik GmbH. The complete operating documentation is openly available: system requirements, installation, configuration and commands. What is still pending today is not the software but the order in which we open new accounts.
View the documentation
What happens after I have submitted the form? +
You receive an email with a confirmation link, valid for 48 hours. Once you have confirmed, the request reaches us and is processed step by step.
How long does it take until I have access? +
Because demand is high, we set up accounts in stages, one request at a time. Anyone who wants to see the platform straight away books a live demo.
Book a live demo
Why do you ask for a work email address? +
Every account is assigned to an organisation, so the form does not accept addresses from public mailbox providers. Companies without a domain of their own are sorted out in a call.
Book a live demo
Will I get advertising or phone calls afterwards? +
No. Your details stay with us and are not shared with anyone. We do not ask for a phone number.
Am I committing to anything if I take part? +
No. There is no obligation to give feedback, no meetings and nothing to sign. You can stop at any time.
Can I not simply install the software myself instead of asking? +
Not yet: the GitHub repository and its publication under the MIT licence are coming soon. The complete installation guide is already openly available. Until then, managed access is the way to work with the platform.
To the installation guide
Starting credit and costs
What exactly is the starting credit of 55 €? +
A one-off credit for the model usage on your account. Every request to a model costs tokens, and those tokens are charged against the credit. For as long as it lasts, no costs arise.
How far do I get with 55 €? +
That depends on the model: short text work is cheap, analysing long documents with the largest models considerably more expensive. For comparison: managed operation includes €8 of model credit per person and month, and the starting credit is more than six times that.
Do I have to provide payment details? +
No, neither for the request nor for the access itself. There is no card on file that would be charged when the credit expires.
What happens when the credit is used up? +
Usage stops, and no invoice arises. That ends the free test phase, and you decide whether managed operation should continue: €15 per person and month, including €8 of model credit per person in your organisation’s shared pool.
View all prices
How do we keep costs under control when billing follows usage? +
Usage is broken down per person, group and model, and a shared monthly budget caps it for the whole organisation. Once it is reached, a soft block takes effect: requests are stopped rather than quietly running on, and the administration can raise the budget or release individual people. An additional monthly limit per person can be set.
Is there a minimum number of users? +
No. Self-hosting is free from a single person upwards and has no seat limit, managed operation is billed per person. There is neither a package for a fixed company size nor a setup fee.
Does the starting credit also apply if we host it ourselves? +
No. It sits on a managed account, because only there does the model usage run through us; with self-hosting you settle directly with your model provider. The form accepts both at once, and a later move from managed operation to your own server is provided for.
Data and confidentiality
Are our inputs used to train models? +
No. Customer data does not train any models, neither at the inference provider nor at our end. Telemetry is switched off by default in all components, and no tracking takes place without active consent.
You offer the large models from OpenAI and Anthropic. Does that mean our data goes to the United States after all? +
Not for storage and inference: conversations, files and accounts are held in Switzerland, and model requests run through EuRouter and are processed in the EU, including models from American vendors. What matters is not only where the data rests, but where the request is computed. There is one exception: web search passes the search query on to external search engines without the identity of the user, so we do not claim across the board that everything stays in Europe.
The data paths in detail
What good is Swiss hosting if the US Cloud Act applies anyway? +
Besides the location, what counts is who controls the operator. Behind EU Cowork AI stands Herr Informatik GmbH in Windisch, Switzerland, with no American parent company; operations run in the data centres of Green in Lupfig. Anyone for whom that is not enough runs the platform on their own hardware.
How long do you store our conversations? +
Out of the box no retention period is set; conversations stay until users or the administration delete them. A period can be configured freely in the admin panel, after which expired content is removed together with its search index entries. Exporting and deleting the data of an individual person is carried out by the administration there as well.
Can anyone at your end read our chats? +
Anyone who self-hosts gives no third party any access. In managed operation the operator accesses the system only for maintenance, governed by the data processing agreement and the list of subprocessors. Inside your instance, users see exactly what their role and group allow, and every access to a connected system is logged.
Do we get a data processing agreement, and who are your subprocessors? +
Yes. The full contract text and the named list of all subprocessors, with purpose and location, are openly available on this website, before signing up and without a sales call.
Read the data processing agreement
Do you have ISO 27001 or SOC 2? +
Certified to ISO 27001 are the data centres of Green in which EU Cowork AI is operated; the certificates are held by Green and not by us. A certification of our own to ISO 27001 is in preparation. The technical and organisational measures are documented openly.
To the measures
We work under professional secrecy. Can we use the tool at all? +
That assessment rests with you and your supervisory body. The basis for it is in place: the data processing agreement, the named list of subprocessors, storage in Switzerland, model processing in the EU and operation on your own hardware. This is not legal advice.
Product and operations
We already have ChatGPT or Microsoft Copilot. Why add something else? +
ChatGPT in the browser is a personal account with no connection to your company systems and no central control, and Copilot is tied to one environment and one model. EU Cowork AI is a company instance with roles, permissions, an audit log and a cost overview, with over 100 models to choose from and with your own systems connected. The models are partly the same; the difference lies in the data path, in the choice and in the control.
The comparison in detail
Why not simply run Open WebUI or LibreChat ourselves? +
That is possible, and EU Cowork AI is itself a thin fork of LibreChat; self-hosting stays free and without a seat limit. On top of that come permissions down to tool level, an audit log, usage and budget with a soft block, prepared integrations and, on request, operation including updates and backup.
Which models do we get, and do we really get the one we chose? +
Over 100 models through one account, among them the large ones from Anthropic, OpenAI, Mistral and Meta. Because every request is processed on the EU side, the catalogue does not have to be limited to European vendors. The administration curates the selection and sets a default model; usage is broken down per model and can therefore be traced.
Can we connect our own documents? +
Yes, as a knowledge base; SharePoint from Microsoft 365 and ERP systems through the MCP gateway are prepared as well. How good the answers turn out depends on the material: cleanly typeset texts work well, scanned forms and nested tables are difficult for any system. A clearly delimited set of documents gives better results at the start than a whole drive.
View all integrations
Do we need an IT department, and how quickly are we ready to start? +
Not for managed operation: the operator handles operation, updates and backup, and you manage users, roles and permissions in the admin panel. The technical part takes minutes. What comes afterwards takes longer: defining roles, connecting systems, working through the first use case. A productive rollout takes days rather than minutes.
Half of our people use ChatGPT privately today. Will this get it under control? +
On a company instance, usage is broken down per person, group and model, every access to a connected system appears in the audit log, and roles determine who sees which models and knowledge sets. How far that visibility reaches is set through roles and permissions; a rule settled in advance makes the rollout easier.
Still something open? To the full collection of questions

# AI platforms compared: 7 providers

URL: https://eucowork.ai/en/vergleich

Market comparison
AI platforms compared: what matters for European companies
Language models have become interchangeable. The difference lies in the data path, in permission control and in licence lock-in. This page compares seven solutions against six criteria taken from everyday work, with a source for every verifiable figure.
In brief
- The market splits into three classes: US cloud services (ChatGPT, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Claude), European SaaS platforms (Langdock) and open source for self-hosting (Open WebUI, LibreChat, EU Cowork AI).
- Seat conditions differ widely: ChatGPT Business requires at least 2 seats, Claude Enterprise at least 20 seats, and Microsoft 365 Copilot requires a qualifying Microsoft 365 licence in addition to its own fee.
- Storage location is where the field separates: Claude workspaces are located in the USA, because “us” is the only available workspace geo. For customers registered in the EU or EFTA, Microsoft 365 Copilot is a service within the EU Data Boundary, with several documented exceptions. OpenAI offers data residency in Europe for new Enterprise and Edu workspaces.
- Open WebUI is published under the “Open WebUI License”, the BSD-3 text with a branding clause: above 50 users in a rolling 30-day period, the branding may only be removed with an enterprise licence or explicit written permission. LibreChat, the basis of EU Cowork AI, is published under MIT.
- EU Cowork AI is open source under MIT, can be self-hosted from a single user upwards with no seat minimum, and is optionally operated in Switzerland. The product is available; access to the managed instance is allocated in stages because demand is high.
As of August 2026. Details based on publicly available information from the respective providers. The sources are numbered at the end of the page.
On this page
- The three classes of AI platform
- Six criteria that make the difference in practice
- The comparison table
- The providers assessed individually
- When each solution fits
- Frequently asked questions
- Sources
The three classes of AI platform
AI platforms for companies fall into three classes: US cloud services, European SaaS platforms and open-source software for self-hosting. The class determines the data path, the pricing model and how dependent a company remains on its provider. The choice of language model almost never determines any of that.
US cloud services
ChatGPT Business and Enterprise, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Claude are finished services with a high level of maturity, a large feature set and per-seat billing. The source code is closed, and operations lie with the provider. For all three, data residency is a matter of configuration or contract, not an architectural property.
European SaaS platforms
Langdock stands for the European SaaS class: operation in the EU, ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II, per-seat billing. 15 The source code remains closed. Operation in your own cloud or your own data centre is available, but according to the provider only from 5,000 seats upwards. 15
Open source for self-hosting
Open WebUI and LibreChat are open-source chat interfaces that you run on your own infrastructure. There is no provider who sees your data, but also none who takes over operations, updates and support. EU Cowork AI is a thin fork of LibreChat under the MIT licence and adds permission management, cost control and managed Swiss hosting as an option to this class. What self-hosting demands in hardware and effort is set out on a page of its own.
Six criteria that make the difference in practice
Six questions decide the selection in practice: where the data is processed, who may access which company data, what growth costs, how large the model selection is, whether your own systems can be connected, and how expensive a change of provider becomes. Everything else is detail.
Where is the data processed?
Storage location is regulated differently across the three US services. For Claude, “us” is currently the only available workspace geo, and it can no longer be changed once the workspace has been created. 12 OpenAI offers data residency for new Enterprise and Edu workspaces as well as for eligible API customers, and now additionally inference residency for the region “Europe (EEA + Switzerland)”. Business workspaces are not covered. 4
For customers who have registered in the EU or in EFTA, Microsoft 365 Copilot is a service within the EU Data Boundary. 7 Microsoft names several exceptions: there are limited cases in which customer data is still transferred outside the boundary, and models provided by Anthropic are currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary. 8 7 On top of that comes “Flex Routing”: model processing may take place in the USA, in Canada or in Australia at peak load, and for tenants created after 25 March 2026 this is active by default. 23
EU Cowork AI runs in ISO 27001 certified data centres operated by Green in Lupfig, Switzerland, and inference is processed on the EU side. The certification is held by the data centre operator; a dedicated ISO 27001 certification of EU Cowork AI is in progress. Anyone self-hosting determines the location entirely themselves.
One limitation no provider can argue away: web search leaves your own infrastructure. With EU Cowork AI, search queries go to external search engines without user identity; with Microsoft 365 Copilot they go to the Bing search service. 7 “Everything stays in Europe” applies to storage and inference, not to the search query itself.
Who may access which company data?
As soon as an AI is connected to a line-of-business system, the decisive question is no longer what the model can do but what the individual employee is allowed to see through it. Providers solve this at three different levels: through existing system permissions, through organisation-wide rules per connector, or through a rule chain of their own ahead of the model.
Microsoft 365 Copilot shows each user only content for which they have at least read permissions in Microsoft 365. 7 That is elegant as long as all relevant data sits in Microsoft 365, and ineffective for everything outside it. With Claude, owners on Team and Enterprise plans can define organisation-wide which actions a connector may perform, for example read-only. 13
EU Cowork AI enforces permissions in the MCP gateway between chat and line-of-business system, down to the individual tool: read invoices yes, read salaries no. Evaluation follows this order: individual user, role, group, server default. Every tool call is written to the audit log and can be exported. How this rule chain works in detail is set out on the governance page.
What does it cost when the team grows?
With all commercial providers the price grows linearly with the number of employees, and with two of them there is an additional lower limit. ChatGPT Business costs 25 US dollars per user and month with monthly payment, 20 US dollars with annual payment, and requires at least 2 seats. 1 According to OpenAI these figures apply in most countries; for Switzerland, OpenAI states CHF 15 per user and month with annual payment. 2 The price for ChatGPT Enterprise is not published. 2
Microsoft 365 Copilot costs 30 US dollars per user and month with annual payment; for smaller companies there is Copilot Business from 18 US dollars per user and month. 24 Both additionally require a separate licence for a qualifying Microsoft 365 plan. 6 Claude Team costs 20 US dollars per seat and month with annual payment and is aimed at teams of 2 to 150 people; Claude Enterprise requires at least 20 seats. 10 11 Langdock states 25 euros per standard seat and month. 14
With open-source software the effort does not depend on the number of people. EU Cowork AI is published under the MIT licence: self-hosting incurs no licence costs, from a single user upwards, with no seat minimum and no mandatory branding. What remains are server costs and language model consumption, both visible in the admin panel per person, group and model.
How many models are available?
Model selection is a lock-in topic, not a quality topic. With ChatGPT and Claude you get the models of the respective house. Microsoft 365 Copilot uses models provided by Microsoft, and administrators additionally decide on the use of third-party models. 7 Langdock describes itself as model-agnostic. 16
EU Cowork AI provides more than 100 models through a single point of access, processed in the EU, including the large models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Mistral and Meta. Your own API key and your own endpoint can be entered by configuration. With Open WebUI and LibreChat you choose the providers entirely yourself, but you also configure them yourself.
Can our own ERP system be connected?
All the platforms compared can connect external systems today, and all of them use the Model Context Protocol in some form for this. ChatGPT supports custom connectors via MCP. 5 With Microsoft the route runs through Copilot Studio, where MCP is generally available. 9 Claude connects through connectors built on MCP. 13
The difference lies not in the protocol but in the control over it. LibreChat can govern access to MCP servers via roles and via a per-server release; individual tools within a server and servers from the configuration file are not covered. 21 22 This is exactly where the MCP gateway of EU Cowork AI comes in: it checks every single tool call, logs the decision and denies if the check errors out instead of letting it through.
What happens when you change provider?
Migration effort is the most frequently overlooked cost item. With closed SaaS services, conversations, prompt collections, agents and connector configurations remain in the provider's system, and pricing is entirely in their hands. With a permissively licensed open-source platform, the software remains usable even once the business relationship ends.
This is exactly where the two open-source options differ. Open WebUI is published under the “Open WebUI License”, the BSD-3 text with an additional branding clause. Above 50 users in a rolling 30-day period, the branding may only be removed or replaced if an enterprise licence or explicit written permission from the rights holder is in place; code up to and including version 0.6.5 remains unaffected under BSD-3. 17 LibreChat, and therefore EU Cowork AI, is published under MIT, without this condition. 20 Why this question matters so much to us is set out on the vision page.

The providers assessed individually
Each of the six solutions has a field in which it is the best choice. The following assessment names the strength first in each case, including where it speaks against EU Cowork AI.
ChatGPT Business and Enterprise
In our assessment, ChatGPT is the most mature product in this comparison and, for many employees, the benchmark against which they measure every other interface. The brand is established, so onboarding is correspondingly short. According to its own statement, OpenAI does not train on business data from Business and Enterprise workspaces by default. 3 Data residency in Europe can be selected for new Enterprise and Edu workspaces. 4
The limits lie where control is required: closed source code, per-seat billing with a lower limit of 2 seats in the Business plan 1 and no way to run the service on your own infrastructure.
Microsoft 365 Copilot
Microsoft 365 Copilot is built into Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint and Teams and shows each user only content for which they have at least read permissions in Microsoft 365. 7 No other product in this comparison reaches that depth. Anyone using Microsoft 365 across the board gets the shortest route from rollout to benefit here.
The price of that depth is lock-in. Copilot costs 30 US dollars per user and month and requires a qualifying Microsoft 365 licence. 6 Outside the Microsoft world the permission logic ends, and for line-of-business systems the route runs through Copilot Studio. 9
Claude
Claude is frequently preferred for long texts, analysis and code, and Anthropic published the Model Context Protocol, which all the providers compared now use. On Team and Enterprise plans, connectors can be restricted organisation-wide, for example to read-only. 13
For European companies with a strict residency requirement, data storage is the sticking point: the workspace geo determines where data rests, and “us” is currently the only available option, which moreover cannot be changed after creation. 12
Langdock
Langdock is the European answer in SaaS format: operation in the EU, ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II, model-agnostic, German-speaking sales. 15 16 For companies that want a finished European platform without running it themselves, this is a serious option.
Two points are relevant for smaller organisations: the standard seat costs 25 euros per month 14 , and operation in your own cloud or on-premise is, according to the provider, only offered from 5,000 seats upwards. 15 The source code remains closed.
Open WebUI and LibreChat
Open WebUI and LibreChat are technically the strongest starting points for teams with their own IT department. Both run on your own hardware, both connect any models, and both are actively developed. LibreChat comes with access control that governs MCP servers via roles and via a per-server release; it does not cover individual tools within a server. 21 22
You should know about two differences. First, the licence: above 50 users in a rolling 30-day period, Open WebUI requires an enterprise licence or written permission from the rights holder if the branding is to be removed. 17 LibreChat is published under MIT. 20 Second, operations: updates, backups, integrations and support are on you.
EU Cowork AI
EU Cowork AI is a thin fork of LibreChat under the MIT licence, extended by the building blocks that cause the most work when built in-house: permissions down to tool level with an audit per call, consumption control with a shared monthly budget and a soft block, roles and groups from Entra ID or maintained locally, and more than 100 models through a single point of access.
Honest about the status: EU Cowork AI is ready for production use, and access to the managed Swiss instance is allocated in stages on request because demand is high. The brand is new, there is no multi-year reference list, and the integration depth in Word, Excel and Outlook does not match that of Microsoft 365 Copilot. The Outlook add-in is in beta and in internal use, the Excel add-in is in progress, native mobile apps are planned, and today the interface is installable as a PWA.
MIT licence
Swiss operation
New brand
When each solution fits
In practice, the selection follows three paths: maximum maturity and integration, European SaaS without running it yourself, or control over data and licence. Each path has a clear winner, and none of them wins all three.
When maturity and integration are decisive
- Your company works entirely in Microsoft 365 and the AI is mainly meant to help in Word, Excel, Outlook and Teams: Microsoft 365 Copilot is the shortest route.
- You need an established product that every employee can operate without training, and processing outside Europe is covered contractually: ChatGPT Business or Enterprise.
- Your focus is on long documents, analysis and code, and storage in the USA has been reviewed and accepted: Claude.
When European operation matters but nobody should look after servers
- You want a finished platform with European operation, certifications and a contract, without your own infrastructure: a European SaaS platform such as Langdock. 15
- You want European operation plus the option of taking the software over yourself later: EU Cowork AI managed, with the MIT licence as a fallback.
When control over data and licence matters
- You have your own IT department and want to build and run everything yourself: LibreChat or Open WebUI directly, with an eye on the branding clause of Open WebUI (see the section on changing provider). 17
- You need permissions down to tool level, an audit per call and cost control, but do not want to develop it yourself: EU Cowork AI, self-hosted or managed.
- You are an IT service provider and operate the platform for several customers: a permissive licence with no seat minimum and no branding obligation is the precondition for that.
When EU Cowork AI does not fit
EU Cowork AI is the wrong choice if your requirement is brand and ecosystem maturity rather than control. Five situations specifically speak against it:
- You need AI directly inside the Microsoft Office applications at full depth: Microsoft 365 Copilot is further ahead there, whereas at EU Cowork AI the Outlook add-in is in beta and the Excel add-in is in progress.
- You expect a native iOS or Android app today: EU Cowork AI is installable as a PWA, native apps are planned. ChatGPT, Claude and Microsoft 365 Copilot deliver native apps today.
- You need a tender response with the provider's own ISO 27001 certification: today the certification is held by the data centre operator, and a dedicated one is in progress. Langdock states ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II for its own operations. 15
- You want an established provider with a long reference list: EU Cowork AI is a young brand and allocates access to the managed instance in stages on request. In that case the three US services and Langdock are the safer answers.
- You do not want to make decisions about roles, groups and tool permissions: governance is the core of this product, and that core requires deliberate setup.
Frequently asked questions
Which European alternative to ChatGPT is there for companies?
For companies there are two European routes: a European SaaS platform such as Langdock with operation in the EU, ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II, or an open-source platform that you run yourself. EU Cowork AI belongs to the second group, is published under the MIT licence and is optionally operated as a managed service in Switzerland.
Is my data processed in Europe with Microsoft 365 Copilot?
For customers who have registered in the EU or in EFTA, Microsoft 365 Copilot is a service within the EU Data Boundary. At the same time Microsoft names several exceptions: limited cases in which data is still transferred outside, models provided by Anthropic, which are currently excluded, and “Flex Routing”, through which model processing may take place in the USA, in Canada or in Australia at peak load. For tenants created after 25 March 2026, Flex Routing is active by default.
Can I use Claude with data storage in Europe?
Not through a Claude workspace directly: the workspace geo determines where data rests, and according to Anthropic documentation “us” is currently the only available option, which cannot be changed after creation. Claude models are reachable in European regions through the platforms of the large cloud providers, which means a different contractual relationship.
What does a self-hosted AI platform cost in licence fees?
With EU Cowork AI, nothing: the software is published under the MIT licence, self-hosting is possible from a single user upwards, with no seat minimum and no mandatory branding. What remains are server costs and language model consumption. With Open WebUI the licence is tied to a condition: above 50 users in a rolling 30-day period, the branding may only be removed with an enterprise licence or written permission from the rights holder.
How does EU Cowork AI differ from LibreChat?
EU Cowork AI is a thin fork of LibreChat under the same MIT licence and adds three building blocks: the MCP gateway, which enforces permissions down to the individual tool and logs every call; cost control with a shared monthly budget and a soft block; and managed hosting in Switzerland as an option. LibreChat itself remains the basis.
Are these details binding?
No. The details on other providers come from their public pricing and product documentation, checked in August 2026, and are linked to their source below. Prices, seat conditions and features change continuously. Check the original source of the respective provider before making a decision.

Questions and answers
Frequently asked questions about EU Cowork AI
41 questions on data protection, operation, features, permissions and licensing, each with a complete answer. EU Cowork AI is ready for production use; access to the managed Swiss instance is allocated in stages because demand is high.
In brief
- EU Cowork AI is operated in ISO 27001 certified data centres run by Green in Lupfig (Switzerland); the certificates are held by Green, and an ISO 27001 certification of EU Cowork AI itself is in progress.
- Customer data does not train any models, telemetry is disabled by default, and every tool call through the MCP gateway is recorded in an exportable audit log.
- More than 100 models are available through a single access point, processed in the EU via EuRouter, including the large models from Anthropic and OpenAI.
- EU Cowork AI is MIT licensed: self-hosting is free from a single user, with no seat limit and no forced branding.
- Permissions reach down to individual tools and are evaluated in the order user, role, group, server default.

Data and privacy: where your data is held and what happens to it
EU Cowork AI is operated in ISO 27001 certified data centres run by Green in Lupfig (Switzerland), model processing takes place in the EU via EuRouter, and customer data does not train any models. Anyone who hosts the software themselves keeps all data on their own infrastructure.
Where is my data processed?
EU Cowork AI is operated in the data centres of Green in Lupfig, Switzerland, and model requests are processed in the EU via EuRouter. Anyone who self-hosts keeps all data entirely on their own infrastructure. The data centres are certified to ISO 27001; the certificates are held by Green and not by EU Cowork AI, and an ISO 27001 certification of EU Cowork AI itself is in progress. The supporting evidence is available in the Trust Center .
Is my data used for training?
No. Customer data does not train any models, neither at the inference provider nor at our end. Telemetry is switched off by default in all components, and no tracking takes place without active consent.
Is our data transferred to the USA?
Not for storage and inference: the data is held in Switzerland, and model requests run through the standard EuRouter access and are processed in the EU, including models from US manufacturers such as Claude and GPT. We name two exceptions openly: web search forwards search queries to external search engines without any user identity, and the administration can additionally connect a deliberately flagged provider outside Europe, for which the EU assurance then does not apply. Anyone who self-hosts chooses every provider in the chain themselves.
Does all data really stay in Europe?
For storage and inference yes, for search queries no. Conversations, files and accounts are held in Switzerland, and model processing takes place in the EU. Web search, by contrast, passes the search query on to external search engines, without the identity of the user. That is why we do not claim across the board that everything stays in Europe.
What happens to our chats if we cancel?
Conversations are held in the database of your own instance and can be exported before shutdown, after which they are deleted. With self-hosting you keep the database anyway and do not have to ask anyone to hand it over. Deadlines and procedures for return and deletion are governed by the data processing agreement .
How long are conversations stored?
Out of the box no retention period is set; one can be configured freely in the admin panel, after which expired content is removed together with its search index entries. Without a set period, conversations remain stored until users or the administration delete them. Exporting and deleting the data of an individual person is likewise carried out by the administration in the admin panel, including full deletion for erasure requests.
Can employees accidentally give company data to the AI?
Yes, employees can type confidential text into any chat tool, including EU Cowork AI. The difference lies in what happens next: the input stays in the instance of your company, does not train any models and is logged. An approved company instance therefore usually works better than a ban that pushes employees onto private accounts.
Do we need a data protection impact assessment?
That depends on the use case, not on the tool: under the GDPR and the revised Swiss FADP an impact assessment is required when processing is likely to result in a high risk to the rights of the data subjects. For that review, EU Cowork AI provides the data processing agreement, the subprocessor list and details of the hosting; a document on the technical and organisational measures is in progress. This answer is not a substitute for legal advice.
Who has access to our data?
Within your instance, users see exactly what their role and group allow, and every access to a connected system is logged. Anyone who self-hosts grants no third party access. In managed operation the operator accesses the system only for maintenance, as governed by the data processing agreement and the subprocessor list .
Does EU Cowork AI collect telemetry or tracking data?
No, telemetry is disabled by default in all components, and no tracking takes place without active consent. Only what you need yourself is logged: logins, administration actions and tool calls in the audit log, plus consumption for the cost overview. This data stays in your instance.
Operation and hosting: who runs the platform and what it requires
EU Cowork AI runs managed in Switzerland, in your own cloud or on your own hardware, always with the same software and without a separate hosting build. Self-hosting is possible today, and the hosted offering is released; access to it is allocated in stages because demand is high.
Which operating models are available?
Three: managed by us in Switzerland, in your own cloud or entirely on your own hardware. In all three cases the same software runs in the same architecture; there is no stripped-down self-host edition. The hosted offering is available; because demand is high, we allocate access in stages via a request .
Does this work without an IT department of our own?
Yes, if you choose the managed option: operation, updates and backups are then handled by the operator, and you only manage users, roles and permissions in the admin panel. For self-hosting you need someone who can set up a Linux server with Docker and keep it up to date. An IT service provider can also take over operation for you.
How quickly is EU Cowork AI set up?
The technical part takes minutes: obtain the package, run an installation script, open the browser. What comes afterwards takes longer: creating users, defining roles and permissions, connecting systems and working through the first use case properly. Plan on days rather than minutes for a productive rollout. The technical procedure is described on the page about self-hosting .
What server do we need for self-hosting?
A small Linux server is enough, because the computing load sits with the model provider and not with you. Measured on the running stack, the base load is around 0.7 GB of memory and the CPU load close to zero in normal operation; budget 1.5 to 2 GB per instance including code execution. For small teams a machine with 4 vCPUs, 16 GB of RAM and an 80 GB disk is enough to run several instances.
Does it also work without internet?
The platform itself runs entirely inside your network, the language models generally do not: requests to a model provider need an internet connection, and web search does in any case. Fully offline operation is only possible with locally hosted models, which requires suitable graphics cards. Such models can be registered as a provider; the model size that runs on your hardware then determines the result you can achieve.
Can several companies run on one server?
Yes, but each company gets its own, fully separated instance: its own database, its own files, its own credentials, its own network and its own environment for code execution. Only uncritical elements such as the container images and an upstream reverse proxy are shared. Up to around 15 users several companies share one machine; above that each company gets its own, as is also the case in regulated industries, where dedicated infrastructure is contractually assured, or when an in-house ERP system is connected.
How do updates and backups work?
Each instance is updated individually, and to a firmly pinned, previously tested version rather than a moving target. A supplied script backs up the database, the configuration and uploaded files into an archive. The same script restores an instance on a different server, which makes a migration a routine operation.
Can we switch from managed operation to self-hosting later on?
Yes, and the other way round as well, because managed operation and self-hosting use the same software in the same architecture. The switch runs via backup and restore on the target server. As the software is MIT licensed, there is no licensing hurdle to slow a switch down.
Features and models: what EU Cowork AI delivers day to day
EU Cowork AI brings together more than 100 models, web search with source references, file generation, a memory and the connection of your own systems in a single interface. The answers below say what of that is running today and what is planned.
What is the difference from ChatGPT in the browser?
ChatGPT in the browser is a personal account with no connection to your company systems and no central control; EU Cowork AI is a company instance with roles, permissions, an audit log and a cost overview. The models are partly the same; the difference lies in the data path and in the controls. On top of that comes the connection of your own systems, so that answers are based on company data rather than on pasted excerpts.
Which models are available?
More than 100 models are available through a single access point, among them the large models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Mistral and Meta. Because every request is processed in the EU, the catalogue does not have to be limited to European manufacturers. The administration can curate the selection and set a default model, so that users are not faced with a long list.
Can we use our own models or our own API keys?
Yes, EU Cowork AI is model-agnostic: any OpenAI-compatible endpoint can be registered by configuration, including your own keys. Locally hosted models are connected the same way. There is no technical lock-in to a single model provider.
Can I connect my ERP system?
Yes, via the MCP gateway. Permissions apply per individual tool and not just per system, and every call is logged. If the identity of the person is also passed through to the ERP system, the existing user permissions there continue to apply; the gateway does not override them. Which systems are prepared is listed on the integrations page.
What is an MCP server?
An MCP server is a bridge that lets an AI platform operate another system; MCP stands for Model Context Protocol, an open standard. The server provides individual tools, for example "read invoice" or "search customer", and permissions are granted at exactly that level. Ready-made MCP servers exist for HubSpot, Slack, Jira, Confluence, Notion, Linear, GitHub, Sentry, PostgreSQL, Stripe and Google Drive; for your own systems a REST API is enough.
Can EU Cowork AI generate Excel, Word and PDF files?
Yes, as soon as the code sandbox is activated for your instance; that is part of the setup. An instruction such as "generate an Excel file for me" is enough, and the finished file is then available for download. The code required for this runs in an isolated environment, not in the browser and not on the machine of the user. An egress proxy with an allow list and additionally hardened isolation of that environment are in progress.
How does EU Cowork AI obtain up-to-date information from the internet?
Through a built-in web search that backs answers with source references and runs on a self-hosted SearXNG. To be open about it: the search query itself is passed on to external search engines, though without the identity of the user. Anyone who does not want that switches web search off.
Does EU Cowork AI remember what matters for our work?
Yes, EU Cowork AI keeps a memory and independently records what will be useful for later answers. The stored entries can be viewed, deleted individually and reside on your own server. Anyone who wants nothing stored at all can disable the feature.
Is there an app?
Today EU Cowork AI can be used as an installable PWA on iPhone, Android devices and the desktop; it launches with its own icon like an app. Native apps for iOS and Android are planned, though no date has been set.
Is EU Cowork AI available directly in Outlook?
Yes, as an add-in in beta. It opens as a pane next to the open email and can summarise, draft a reply, translate between German and English and extract tasks with owners and deadlines. Today it is in internal use at our company and not yet generally available; the rollout will follow together with the Excel add-in. Until then everything runs through the browser, with the same range of functions, only the route is longer.
Who is liable if the AI says something wrong?
Language models can produce false output, which is why answers are drafts and not verified information; responsibility for using a result remains with the company working with it. EU Cowork AI reduces the risk through source references in web search, through answers based on real company data rather than on the memory of the model, and through a log of every data access. What applies contractually is set out in the terms and conditions ; this answer is not a substitute for legal advice.
Permissions, roles and costs: who may do what and what it consumes
EU Cowork AI controls access and costs upstream of the model: permissions apply down to individual tools, every call is recorded in the audit log, and a shared monthly budget caps consumption across the entire organisation.
Who in the company may see which company data?
That is decided by a rule chain upstream of the model, not by the model itself: the check runs in the order individual user, role, group and server default, and the first match wins. If the check fails, access is denied rather than granted. You maintain roles and groups in the admin panel or take them from Entra ID. How this chain is structured in detail is described on the governance page.
How do we prevent the AI from seeing payroll data?
By not releasing the tool in question: permissions apply per individual tool and not per system, so "read invoices yes, salaries no". In addition, the permissions of the source system continue to apply, so that two independent checks take effect. Every call is logged with person, tool and decision.
Where do roles and groups come from?
Maintained locally in the admin panel or taken from Entra ID, depending on whether an identity service is in place. Sign-in via Entra ID or another OIDC provider is supported by the platform and set up per instance; users are then created automatically on first sign-in and their groups are taken over. Automatic provisioning and deactivation via SCIM is planned; today the rule is: no account in the directory, no login.
What does the audit log contain?
Every tool call through the MCP gateway, every administration action and every login, each with person, timestamp and decision. The log can be exported and is therefore usable as evidence for auditors or data protection authorities. Entries are appended continuously and not overwritten.
How do we keep AI costs under control?
Consumption is reported per person, group and model, in tokens and in euros, and a shared monthly budget for the entire organisation caps it. Instead of tight individual limits, all users share the same pot, which avoids frustration about arbitrary boundaries. An additional monthly limit per person can be set if you want one.
What happens when the monthly budget is used up?
A soft block takes effect: requests are stopped instead of quietly continuing, and the administration can raise the budget or release individual people specifically. Exceeding the budget without notice is not provided for. That way there is no invoice at the end of the month that nobody authorised.
What are role agents, and who releases them?
Role agents are prepared AI coworkers for recurring tasks, for example for proposal texts or evaluations, with defined instructions and tools. They are released per group by the administration and not by each user individually. This keeps control over who uses which agent and therefore which data sources.
Open source and licensing: what MIT means in practice
EU Cowork AI is MIT licensed and a thin fork of LibreChat. Self-hosting is free from a single user, with no seat limit and no forced branding.
Is this really open source?
Yes. EU Cowork AI is MIT licensed and a thin fork of LibreChat. Self-hosting is free from a single user, with no seat limit and no forced branding. The LibreChat base is publicly available today, is MIT licensed and has more than 40,000 stars on GitHub; the GitHub repository with our extensions and its publication under MIT are coming soon. After that the code can be inspected, modified and passed on, including for commercial purposes.
What does the MIT licence mean in practice?
You may use, modify and pass on the software and build it into your own products, as long as the licence text is retained. There is no user limit, no forced branding and no features locked behind an enterprise barrier. This is where MIT differs from licences that require your own branding or a commercial licence above a certain number of users.
Is self-hosting really free?
Yes, the software is free and has no user limit, starting from a single person. What you bear is your server and the model provider you choose, both independent of us. Managed operation costs €15 per person and month, CHF 14 in Switzerland, of which €8 and CHF 7.50 respectively are model credit in your organisation’s shared pool. All details on this are on the pricing page.
What is the difference between EU Cowork AI and LibreChat?
EU Cowork AI is a thin fork of LibreChat, extended by what companies additionally need: an MCP gateway with permissions down to tool level, an admin panel with a cost overview and a shared budget, and a ready-made operating package. The fork deliberately stays close to the original so that new developments from LibreChat continue to flow in. On top of that come German-language support and the option of handing over operation entirely.
Who is behind EU Cowork AI?
Behind EU Cowork AI stands Herr Informatik GmbH in Windisch, Switzerland, which uses the platform internally itself. Anyone who only wants to run the software themselves does not need a contract with us. Why we are building the product is explained on the vision page.
Still have a question?
The hosted Swiss instance is running. Because demand is high, we allocate access in stages; afterwards you can clarify open questions directly on your own instance.
Get started
Self-host

# Security, data protection, data residency

Trust Center
Security, data protection and data residency
EU Cowork AI is operated in ISO 27001-certified data centres run by Green in Lupfig, Switzerland, while the language models run on the EU side via EuRouter. Every statement on this page is either substantiated or explicitly marked as in progress.
In short
- Conversations, files and accounts reside in ISO 27001-certified data centres run by Green in Lupfig, Switzerland. The certificates are held by Green, not by EU Cowork AI.
- Requests to the language models are routed through EuRouter, a European gateway to more than 100 models. Every request is processed in the EU, and the content is not retained there by default.
- Customer data does not train any models, and telemetry is switched off by default.
- Web search forwards search queries to external search engines without any user identity. “Everything stays in Europe” applies to storage and inference, not to the search query itself.
- Anyone who self-hosts EU Cowork AI keeps all data on their own infrastructure. In self-hosted operation, all subprocessors are eliminated apart from the model providers you choose yourself.
On this page
- Where your data resides
- What does not happen to your data
- Which law applies to your data
- Technical and organisational measures
- Certifications: where we stand today
- Which documents you receive today
- Frequently asked questions
Where your data resides
In operation managed by EU Cowork AI, conversations, uploaded files, accounts and logs reside in ISO 27001-certified data centres run by Green in Lupfig, Switzerland. Requests to the language models are processed in the EU via EuRouter. Anyone who self-hosts EU Cowork AI keeps all of this data on their own infrastructure.
Storage location per data type, in managed operation and in self-hosted operation.

Self-hosted operation

Operation in Switzerland
Managed operation of EU Cowork AI takes place in the data centres run by Green in Lupfig, canton of Aargau, Switzerland, which are certified to ISO 27001. This certification is held by Green as the data centre operator, not by EU Cowork AI. Swiss data protection law therefore applies to the stored data, namely the revised Federal Act on Data Protection.
Where the models compute
The language models do not run on the chat server but at the inference provider. EU Cowork AI uses EuRouter for this, a European gateway to more than 100 models: every request is processed in the EU, and request content is not retained by default and is not used for training. What the provider does retain is usage metadata such as timestamps and token counts, for up to twelve months.
This applies to standard access via EuRouter. An additional provider outside Europe can be connected; where this is the case in your instance, your administration discloses it, and the EU assurance does not apply to that provider.
What applies in self-hosted operation
In self-hosted operation, no content leaves your infrastructure apart from the model requests sent to the provider you have chosen. Database, search index, file storage and logs reside on your server, as do the access keys. All subprocessors are eliminated, except for the model providers you enter yourself. EU Cowork AI is MIT-licensed, with no seat limit and no mandatory branding.
What does not happen to your data
Customer data does not train any models, telemetry is switched off by default, and there is no tracking without active consent. One exception is named in the section on web search further below.
No training on your data
Customer data is not used to train models. This is set out in the data processing agreement and in the general terms and conditions of EU Cowork AI, and it also applies to the inference provider EuRouter, which does not retain request content by default. A standalone no-training statement as a separate document is in progress.
Telemetry off by default
All platform components ship with telemetry disabled, including the search index and the chat application itself. The instance reports no usage statistics to third parties and is not released to search engines. This default applies in managed operation as well as in self-hosted operation and does not need to be switched off first.
Being honest about web search
Web search in EU Cowork AI runs through a self-hosted search instance based on SearXNG. This instance forwards the search query to external search engines, without user identity, without an account and without profiling. The statement “everything stays in Europe” therefore applies to storage and inference, not to the search query itself.
Anyone who does not want this forwarding switches web search off in the admin panel. The rest of the platform continues to work without it. We name this point rather than glossing over it, because an assurance is only worth as much as its exceptions.
Which law applies to your data
EU Cowork AI is subject to the revised Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection (revFADP) and to the GDPR, both contractually assured. For managed operation, customer and provider conclude a data processing agreement under Art. 28 GDPR. The subprocessors used are listed publicly and form part of that agreement.
What the revised FADP means here
Managed operation takes place in Switzerland and is therefore subject to the revised Federal Act on Data Protection. The provider of EU Cowork AI is Herr Informatik GmbH, domiciled in Windisch, Switzerland. What is processed is the content that users enter into the service, as well as account metadata. The data subjects are the customer’s employees and contacts.
When the GDPR applies in addition
The GDPR applies in addition as soon as data of persons in the EU is processed. EU Cowork AI processes personal data exclusively to provide the agreed service and only on documented instructions from the customer. Processing outside the EU, the EEA and Switzerland does not take place without appropriate safeguards.
Data processing and subprocessors
The data processing agreement governs the binding effect of instructions, confidentiality, support with data subject rights and notification obligations. It is available today as a complete structural preview; the signature-ready version is under legal review and therefore in progress. The list of subprocessors is part of the agreement: changes are announced in advance, and you can assert legitimate objections.
After the contract ends, customer data is exported on request and subsequently deleted, insofar as no statutory retention obligation applies. A retention period for conversations can be set freely in the admin panel; once it expires, content is removed together with its search index entries. Export and deletion of an individual person’s data is likewise carried out there by the administration, including full deletion for erasure requests. How this works in day-to-day practice is described on the Governance page.
Technical and organisational measures
The following measures are implemented in the product or are binding requirements for operation; they apply to managed operation as well as to self-hosted operation. Where a measure is set by the operator, the row says so. This overview is the current public version. A standalone TOM document as an annex to the data processing agreement is in progress and will be linked here as soon as it is available.
Technical and organisational measures, implemented in the product or mandated in operation. As at: August 2026.
Area
Implementation
Transmission
TLS for all connections. Certificates are issued and renewed automatically by the bundled reverse proxy.
Data at rest
The data resides on the operator’s machine. For managed operation, encryption of the storage media is part of server provisioning; in self-hosted operation it is the operator’s responsibility.
Access control
Roles and groups, with permissions down to individual tools. Evaluation follows this order: individual user, role, group, server default.
Behaviour on failure
If the permission check fails, access is denied, not granted.
Identity
Local accounts with invitation and a self-chosen password. Sign-in via Entra ID or another OIDC provider with role and group claims is supported by the platform and is set up per instance; anyone blocked there can no longer get in. Without a configured directory service, local user management applies.
Logging
Every tool call through the MCP gateway, every administrative action and every login is logged, continuously chained, tamper-evident after the fact and exportable.
Customer separation
One dedicated stack per customer with its own database, its own search index, its own file storage, its own configuration, its own network and its own inference key. None of this is shared between customers. This separation is a binding requirement for managed operation and is set when each instance is provisioned.
Code execution
Code generated by the user runs in a short-lived, isolated environment per session, with a dedicated network per customer and hard resource and time limits.
Software versions
The application image is pinned to its digest rather than to a moving tag; the remaining services run on fixed versions. A release is therefore a tested, reproducible combination.
Secrets
Credentials and keys are generated during installation, never reside in the source code and are separated per customer.
Backup
Backup per customer covering database, configuration and files. The same tool serves for restore and for migration to another server.
Server hardening
The setup script configures the firewall, automatic security updates and log rotation. For public operation, the chat service is bound to the local interface, so that only the reverse proxy is reachable from outside.
Auditability
The platform builds on LibreChat, which is publicly available under the MIT licence. Our own extensions will likewise be published under MIT, coming soon. Assurances can then be verified against the code and the configuration.
Access is decided before the model
It is not the language model that decides which company data it may see, but a chain of rules ahead of it. Calls to a connected system run through the MCP gateway, which checks the requesting user’s permissions and logs the decision. Authorisations are possible per system and per individual tool: read invoices yes, read salaries no. Where the person’s identity is instead passed through to the target system, that system enforces its own permissions. How roles, groups, logging and budget interact in detail is described on the Governance page.
What is not yet implemented today
Three points are open and are named here rather than passed over. An egress proxy with an allow list for network access from the code sandbox is in progress. The strongest isolation level of the code sandbox requires virtualisation support on the server and is therefore not the default everywhere. Automatic provisioning and blocking of accounts via SCIM is planned; today blocking is handled through the directory service.
Certifications: where we stand today
EU Cowork AI does not hold a certification of its own today. The ISO 27001 certification on which operation relies is held by the data centre operator Green in Lupfig. An ISO 27001 certification of EU Cowork AI itself is in progress. A SOC 2 report is not available and is currently not planned.
ISO 27001 at the data centre: in place
Own ISO 27001: in progress
SOC 2: not available
This distinction matters for your own assessment: Green’s certification covers the data centre, meaning the building, power, cooling, physical access and physical security. It does not cover the application and its operation. For that layer, the self-declaration on this page applies today, backed by the contractual assurances and by the open code base LibreChat on which the platform is built.
Which documents you receive today
Four documents are available today: the data processing agreement, the subprocessor list, the privacy policy and the general terms and conditions. Four more are in progress and will be linked here as soon as they are available. Until then, we provide written information on each of these points on request.
Available today
- Data processing agreement : processing of personal data under Art. 28 GDPR and the revised FADP. Structural preview; the signature-ready version is under legal review.
- Subprocessors : current list of sub-processors, forming part of the data processing agreement.
- Privacy policy : handling of personal data under the revised FADP and the GDPR.
- General terms and conditions : contractual terms for use of the service, including the no-training assurance.
In progress, without a link
These four items do not yet exist as standalone documents and therefore appear without a link. As soon as one of them is available, it will be linked here. Until then, we provide written information on each point on request. Shorter answers to recurring questions can be found in the frequently asked questions .

- Hosting fact sheet on the data centre in Lupfig.
- No-training statement as a standalone declaration.

Frequently asked questions
Is our data transferred to the USA?
No. Conversations, files and accounts reside in Switzerland, and model requests are processed in the EU via EuRouter. Processing outside the EU, the EEA and Switzerland does not take place without appropriate safeguards. If your administration deliberately connects an additional provider outside Europe, this assurance does not apply to that provider.
Do the language models train on our company data?
No. Customer data does not train any models. This is set out in the data processing agreement and in the general terms and conditions, and it also applies to the inference provider EuRouter, which does not retain request content by default. A standalone no-training statement as a separate document is in progress.
Does everything really stay in Europe, including web search?
No, and we say so openly. Storage and inference remain in Switzerland and the EU. Web search runs through a self-hosted search instance that forwards search queries to external search engines, without user identity. Anyone who does not want this switches web search off in the admin panel.
Is EU Cowork AI certified to ISO 27001?
No. The ISO 27001 certification is held by the data centre operator Green in Lupfig, in whose data centres EU Cowork AI is operated. It covers the data centre, not the application. An ISO 27001 certification of EU Cowork AI itself is in progress; a SOC 2 report is not available.
What happens to our data if we terminate the contract?
After the contract ends, customer data is exported on request and subsequently deleted, insofar as no statutory retention obligation applies. In self-hosted operation the question does not arise: the data is on your infrastructure anyway, and backup and deletion are your responsibility.
Do we need a data processing agreement?
Yes, as soon as EU Cowork AI is managed by us and personal data of your company is processed in the course of that. The agreement under Art. 28 GDPR and the revised FADP is available as a structural preview; the signature-ready version is under legal review. In self-hosted operation no data processing agreement with us is required, because no data flows to us.
Hold us to our word
Request access to the managed Swiss instance now, or run EU Cowork AI on your own server. The GitHub repository under the MIT licence is coming soon, after which every assurance can be verified against the code.
