AI in everyday work
AI in manufacturing: keeping the knowledge when the people leave
The experienced people are retiring, and the demands of large customers keep arriving: questionnaires, audit catalogues, evidence. This article walks through three workflows to show how an AI colleague works with the knowledge of your plant, and where the line to the machine runs.
Manufacturing
18 August 2026
Reading time: 11 minutes
- Starting point
- The workforce’s knowledge
- Audits and questionnaires
- Instructions in every language
- Connectors to your ERP
- Data protection and secrets
- Frequently asked questions
In brief
- German manufacturing still employed 5.29 million people in mid-2026, 144,100 fewer than a year earlier. 1 In Norway, 62% of the industry association’s member companies report unmet skills needs. 4
- EU Cowork AI works with the knowledge of your plant. Service reports, fault and inspection records, setup sheets and past audit answers become a knowledge base: a collection of your own documents that you can question in plain sentences. Every answer names the document it comes from.
- For customer audits and supplier questionnaires you get a gap list and draft answers from your own documentation. Approval happens in the business; no software fulfils compliance.
- An ERP such as Monitor ERP, RamBase or weclapp can be connected if it has a documented interface. An interface is the point where two programs exchange data; the Model Context Protocol (MCP) is the open standard an AI program uses to reach it. Permissions per tool and a log for every access apply. The machine and MES layer, that is controllers and production control, is left out.
On this page
- Starting point
- The workforce’s knowledge
- Audits and questionnaires
- Instructions in every language
- Connectors to your ERP
- Data protection and secrets
- Frequently asked questions
Starting point: the knowledge leaves, the evidence obligations arrive
At the end of the first half of 2026, German manufacturing employed 5.29 million people, 144,100 or 2.7% fewer than a year earlier. 1 The documentation has not shrunk with it, it is simply spread across fewer shoulders.
It looks similar across Europe. In Sweden, 87% of the technology and industrial companies surveyed report difficulties recruiting skills in electrical engineering, energy and automation. 2 In Norway, 62% of the member companies of Norsk Industri report unmet skills needs and name lost market share as a consequence. 4 In Spain, official statistics counted 13,868 vacancies in industry alone in the fourth quarter of 2025. 6
From the other direction come the requirements. The German supply chain due diligence act applies to companies with, as a rule, at least 1,000 employees in Germany. Until the start of 2024 the threshold stood at 3,000. 7 The supplier with 60 people is not covered, but the questionnaires of its large customers land on its desk anyway. Cybersecurity follows the same pattern: in Italy the NIS2 baseline measures must be in place by October 2026, and whoever supplies affected customers receives the requirements by contract. 8
With AI itself, the biggest gap runs not between countries but between large and small. In Sweden, 30.7% of companies with 10 to 49 employees use at least one AI technology, against 71.9% from 250 employees upwards. 3 In France, only 15% of the small and medium-sized businesses in the food industry, the country’s leading industrial sector, use AI solutions. 5
1
2
3
- Experience leaves the business, shift by shift
- Same plant, same documentation, fewer people
- Questionnaires, audit catalogues and evidence from customers
Two movements meet in the same office: the knowledge leaves, the requirements arrive. Both land with the same people.
Use case 1: the knowledge of the retiring generation becomes queryable
The maintenance technician who has known for twenty years how this press behaves after a tool change retires in two years. Much of his knowledge is already inside the company, just scattered: in service reports, fault and inspection records, setup sheets and the handwritten settings in the folder next to the machine. A knowledge base built from those documents answers the night shift’s question. It names the source, that is the document and the page the answer comes from: which setting worked for this batch last time, how was this fault fixed.
The difference to a chat in the browser is the reference. The answer comes from your documents and shows which report it came from. It does not come from the model’s memory, that is from what the program learned in general. What is not written down it will not find, and outdated documents produce outdated answers.
1
2
3
- A question from the shift, in everyday language
- The plant’s service reports, inspection records and setup sheets
- An answer with its source, checkable in seconds
The knowledge base answers from the plant’s documents and shows which report the answer came from.
What the AI colleague does not do: it does not set up any machine. It shows what was set last time and who documented it. The decision is made at the machine.
Use case 2: preparing customer audits and supplier questionnaires
A large customer sends a supplier questionnaire with 120 items: supply chain due diligence, proof of origin, information security. In parallel, preparation for the next IFS or BRCGS audit is running. Almost every answer is already somewhere inside the company, in last year’s self-declaration, in a certificate, in a procedure. It is just that nobody finds it in the week before the deadline.
The AI colleague maps the questions to the existing documents, produces a gap list for everything with no evidence on file, and files draft answers with source references for the rest. The work shifts from searching to reviewing. The gap list is often the bigger gain: it shows before the audit what is missing.
1
2
3
4
- The customer’s questionnaire and audit catalogue
- Certificates, procedures and earlier answers
- Gap list: what the company has nothing on file for
- Draft answers with source references, for technical approval
The answers are usually already inside the company. The draft makes them findable; every statement is owned by the business.
This is the sharpest limit. Every answer in a supplier questionnaire is a commitment to your customer, every audit document is evidence towards a certification body. Both go out after technical approval, never automatically.
Use case 3: instructions, labels and manuals in the language of the shift
In food production and in assembly, shift teams work in mixed languages. The hygiene rule, the setup instruction and the short version of the operating manual are generated from the approved document in the language of the employees. The key element is a company glossary: machine names, part designations and technical terms are fixed once, so that the same assembly is not called something different in every version.
The same glossary carries the declaration and label texts and the operating manual for export. It carries the other way too: the Spanish supplier specification and the Italian test certificate become readable without an outside translation portal.
1
2
3
- The plant’s approved source document
- Company glossary: machine names, parts, technical terms
- Language versions as drafts, for approval by the qualified person
The glossary fixes the terms so that the same assembly does not end up with a different word in every language.
The limit applies here too: translations are drafts. For safety-relevant briefings and legally required information, the approved version remains authoritative, and it is the qualified person who approves it. Permissions apply down to individual tools: whoever may not see the costing does not see it through the AI either. Every access is recorded in the audit log, a record of who opened which document and when.
Connectors: what can be linked to your ERP
An AI colleague is only as useful as what it is allowed to reach. MCP is an open standard that lets an AI program address another program. What it needs is a documented interface, that is a published connection point where two programs exchange data. Every single tool is released separately, and every call is logged. Default setting: reading tools free, writing tools only with confirmation. The table shows how far the AI connection to common software reaches today, checked in August 2026. The middle column gives the technical names of those interfaces; the column that matters for you is the right one.
Software (country)
Interface

API documentation openly accessible, REST for queries

What you deliberately will not find here: the machine and MES layer, that is production control. Controllers, shop floor data capture and detailed scheduling were not examined. An integration promise that breaks in the first conversation costs more than it brings. The benefit arises in the office and in work preparation. If your software is missing, the knowledge base and audit preparation still work: they only need documents. More under integrations .
The separation also has a legal reason. If AI is built into a regulated product as a safety component, it can qualify as a high-risk system under the AI Regulation. Under Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 its obligations apply from 2 December 2027, and from 2 August 2028 for embedded systems. 9 An assistant in the office does not normally fall under this.
Data protection and secrecy: specifications stay in the plant
Customer specifications, recipes, costings and inspection data are trade secrets, often bound by a non-disclosure agreement with your customer on top. For personal data the General Data Protection Regulation applies. The business remains responsible even when an AI tool processes it. If a provider is involved, that requires a data processing agreement, a contract setting out what this provider may do with the data. This article is not legal advice.
If data goes to a country outside Europe, Chapter V of the Regulation applies as well. You then need a legal basis for the transfer and, depending on the instrument you choose, an assessment of the legal situation in the destination country. If storage and model processing take place within the European Economic Area, that step falls away. This does not make the processing lawful automatically, but it does make it easier to justify.
EU Cowork AI runs in ISO 27001 certified data centres or on your own server. Model requests are processed in the EU, and customer data does not train any models. Telemetry, that is the reporting back of usage data, is switched off by default. If nothing at all may go outside, you run your own instance in your own data centre. An instance is the installation that runs for your company alone. The software is MIT licensed. The data processing agreement and the subprocessor list are published openly on the website.
One more point the European statistics show clearly: in Norway, 71% of AI-using companies rely on off-the-shelf software, in Sweden 62%. 3 Such tools are available quickly, but they do not know the business: no service reports, no inspection records, no audit answers.
Frequently asked questions from manufacturing and food production
Can the AI control our machines or set parameters, or does it only work with the ERP and documents?
It controls nothing. EU Cowork AI is office support: searching documents, writing drafts and querying systems with a documented interface, for instance Monitor ERP, weclapp, SAP Business One or Odoo. The machine and MES layer, that is controllers and production control, is deliberately left out. AI in a safety function is a different product class.
Does this fulfil our audit obligations, for example under IFS, BRCGS or HACCP?
No. The AI colleague prepares: it finds the existing records, shows gaps and writes draft answers. Verification, approval and responsibility for the HACCP plan stay in the business. Compliance is fulfilled by people, not by software.
How does the knowledge of experienced staff get into the knowledge base?
Through what is already written down: service reports, fault and inspection records, setup sheets, procedures and audit reports. What only exists in someone’s head has to be written down or dictated first. This is not a substitute for being trained in.
Do we have to do anything because of the AI Regulation?
For an internal assistant, the Regulation as a rule provides for no approval or conformity obligations. Two things apply to every deployer: ensuring a sufficient level of AI literacy, and disclosing when people are interacting with an AI system. Caution applies as soon as a tool decides about people, for instance when pre-sorting job applications. This answer is not legal advice.
What does it cost for a plant with eighty people?
Managed operation costs €15 per person per month. Of that, €8 is model credit: a shared pot for your organisation that pays for the requests to the language model. If you self-host, the software costs nothing: it is MIT licensed, a free licence with no licence fee. All details on the pricing page.
Where is our data held?
In the managed variant in ISO 27001 certified data centres, otherwise on your own server. Customer data does not train any models and model requests are processed in the EU. Evidence in the Trust Center .

# AI for tax and law firms in Europe: DATEV

AI in everyday work
Fewer professionals, more rules: three AI workflows in the firm
Opening a new file, passing on the firm’s knowledge, guiding clients through the deadlines: the profession is shrinking while the rulebooks keep growing. This article walks through three workflows to show how an AI colleague works with your own documents and where the limits run.
Fiduciary and legal
18 August 2026
Reading time: 10 minutes
- Starting point
- Opening a client file
- Firm knowledge, queryable
- Guiding clients through deadlines
- The limits
- Connectors to firm software
- Data protection
- Frequently asked questions
In brief
- The profession is shrinking while the rulebooks grow: in Germany the chambers count 53,932 tax advisory practices, a good two thirds of them sole practices, with an average age of 53.7 years. 1
- EU Cowork AI works with your firm’s own documents. Client files, briefing notes, model letters and guidelines become a knowledge base: a collection you can question in plain language. Every answer names its source.
- The platform does not advise, it prepares. The German statutory reservation on tax advice under Section 5 StBerG, professional secrecy and sign-off by a qualified professional all remain untouched. 9
- Your data stays on your own server or in a European data centre, and it does not train any models.
On this page
- Starting point
- Opening a client file
- Firm knowledge, queryable
- Guiding clients through deadlines
- The limits
- Connectors to firm software
- Data protection
- Frequently asked questions
Starting point: the profession is shrinking, the rulebooks are growing
In Germany the tax advisers’ chambers count 53,932 practices, a good 67% of them sole practices, with an average age of 53.7 years. Training contracts for tax clerks fell to 17,081, down 1.3%, while the number of career changers in retraining rose to 2,113. 1 In Italy the profession is shrinking outright: at the end of 2025, 119,050 dottori commercialisti and esperti contabili were registered, 0.8% fewer than the year before, with a median income of 48,420 euros against an average of 87,376 euros. 2
In Liechtenstein the supervisor names the connection itself: in its supervisory priorities for 2026, the FMA writes that the number of providers in the fiduciary sector is declining slightly in the face of tightened regulation and a high regulatory workload. 3 In Sweden the bottleneck sits on the other side: Srf konsulterna counts the redovisningskonsult among the shortage occupations, with around 70,000 company formations a year. 4
At the same time, the rulebooks are arriving almost all at once. In France, from 1 September 2026 every VAT-registered business must be able to receive electronic invoices and from 1 September 2027 small businesses must also send them, through a plateforme agréée, a state-approved invoicing platform. 6 In Spain, entities subject to corporate income tax must adapt their invoicing systems before 1 January 2027 and all others before 1 July 2027. The B2B obligation from Real Decreto 238/2026 only starts running with a ministerial order that is still outstanding, and then twelve or twenty-four months respectively. 7 In Norway the amendments to the bookkeeping act take effect in stages: electronic invoicing between businesses subject to bookkeeping obligations from 1 January 2027, electronic bookkeeping from 1 January 2030. 8 In Italy it has long been routine through the Sistema di Interscambio.
Each of these deadlines is two things at once: an advisory mandate and an administrative load in your own office. That technology is not the bottleneck is clear from the European statistics: in 2025, 55.0% of EU enterprises with 250 or more employees used at least one AI technology, but only 17.0% of those with 10 to 49 employees. 5 That gap is wider than any gap between countries.
Use case 1: opening a client file instead of leafing through it
A new engagement arrives with four binders and two years of correspondence. The AI colleague reads what you give it and builds a chronology: who decided what and when, which contracts and amendments exist, which deadlines they name and which points remain open. Every entry comes with its source.
The same helps in an ongoing engagement: an overview of the state of play before a meeting, the requested documents drafted before an audit, a summary of a long assessment notice. What the assistant does not do is judge. It shows where something is written, not what follows from it.
1
2
3
- Files, contracts and correspondence of the engagement
- A chronology with the people involved and the sources
- Open points, named instead of overlooked
The assistant orders what is there and names the source for every entry. The assessment happens in the firm.
Deadline control stays in your practice management software and with a person. A date found in a document is a prompt to check, not a confirmed deadline.
Use case 2: the firm’s knowledge becomes queryable
Anyone starting out asks the same first question: how do we do this here? While training contracts in Germany are declining, the number of career changers in retraining is rising. 1 Career changers bring professional experience, but not the knowledge of this particular firm. A knowledge base built from briefing notes, model letters and past correspondence answers such questions with a source reference, instead of interrupting an experienced colleague for the twelfth time.
Permissions apply right down to individual folders. Whoever does not work on an engagement does not see it through the assistant either, and every access is recorded in the log. That is the condition under which a knowledge base can be reconciled with client confidentiality.
1
2
3
- A question in everyday language, including from new staff
- Briefing notes, model letters and guidelines, with permissions per folder
- An answer with its source, checkable in seconds
The knowledge base answers from the firm’s own documents. What someone may not see, they do not see through the assistant either.
The gain is twofold: experienced staff are interrupted less often, and the knowledge stays in the firm when someone retires. The knowledge base is only as good as the documents in it.
Use case 3: guiding clients through the deadlines
Every one of these deadlines creates the same work: explaining, reminding, following up. A circular on electronic invoicing, a query about missing documents, thirty times in a slightly different version. The assistant draws the draft from your own technical notes, groups engagements by who is affected, and files the letters for review.
In cross-border engagements language is added: from the German briefing note, the French, Italian or Spanish version is drafted, with the same source references. For legally relevant letters the translation remains a draft, never the binding text.
1
2
3
4
- The firm’s technical note or briefing note on the new obligation
- One input, several versions by engagement and language
- Drafts in the firm’s tone, with the same source references
- Sign-off by the qualified professional, and only then dispatch
One technical note becomes many letters. None of them leaves the firm without sign-off.
What deliberately does not happen: nothing is transmitted automatically to a government system, not to the Sistema di Interscambio, not to VERI*FACTU and not to a plateforme agréée. The assistant prepares, a person transmits.
The limits, plainly stated
In Germany, providing assistance in tax matters on a commercial basis is reserved to the persons named in Sections 3, 3a, 3d and 4 StBerG. Section 5 StBerG prohibits it for everyone else. 9 EU Cowork AI therefore gives neither tax nor legal advice. The platform prepares the answer and replaces neither the professional nor an expert-comptable, a commercialista or a gestoría.
Professional secrecy is the second fixed point: secret professionnel in France, segreto professionale in Italy, secreto profesional in Spain, and the duty of confidentiality under professional law in Germany, Austria and Liechtenstein. It carries criminal sanctions, and a data processing agreement does not set it aside. The responsibility stays in the firm. Three sentences follow: a language model can produce errors, which is why every text is a draft. Every source reference is checked against the original. And compliance is never automatically fulfilled; it arises through people and processes.
Connectors: what can be linked to your firm software
An AI colleague is only as useful as what it is allowed to reach. The link to another program is called a connector. It runs over MCP, an open standard for connecting external systems. The prerequisite is a documented interface, an API in technical language: the vendor publicly describes how other programs may retrieve data. Some vendors already ship a ready-made connecting piece for this, an MCP server. Permissions apply per tool, and every call is logged. The state of play for common practice management and accounting software, checked in August 2026: For the Spanish practice-management suites no verified findings are available, which is why they have no row in this table.
Software (country)
Interface
Connection to EU Cowork AI

The pattern is the same in all eight markets: what is open is usually the accounting system, what is closed is the large practice suite. Is your software missing? Most of the daily work runs without any system connection. How the AI connection to a practice management or accounting software works via MCP is described on the integrations page.
Data protection: client data stays where you want it
EU Cowork AI runs on your own server or managed in data centres with ISO 27001 certification. Customer data does not train any models, model processing takes place in the EU, and the data processing agreement and subprocessor list are published openly on this website.
Factually, one point matters most. If personal data is transferred to a third country, that is a country outside the European Economic Area, Chapter V of the General Data Protection Regulation applies. That means its own legal basis and, depending on the instrument, an assessment of the legal situation there. If storage and model processing stay within the European Economic Area, that step falls away. What remains is processing on behalf of a controller under Article 28, which every firm already handles. Nothing becomes automatically lawful that way, but it becomes easier to justify.
The second point is fit. In 2025, 71.0% of AI-using enterprises in Norway and 62.1% in Sweden used commercial software bought off the shelf. 5 Such tools are useful, but they do not know your own firm: not your client files, not your model letters. That is precisely where the difference lies.
Frequently asked questions from tax, law and fiduciary firms
May the platform give my clients tax or legal advice?
No. In Germany, assistance in tax matters on a commercial basis is reserved under Section 5 StBerG to those authorised to provide it. Comparable professional reservations apply in the other target markets. The assistant finds passages, summarises and drafts. The assessment and the sign-off stay with the qualified professional. This article is not legal advice.
How does this work with professional secrecy?
Professional secrecy carries criminal sanctions in France, Italy and Spain and is protected under professional and criminal law in the German-speaking markets. A data processing agreement does not set it aside. It is the basis on which a service provider may be brought in at all.
We work with DATEV. Does EU Cowork AI work with it?
Yes. Connecting to DATEV runs through the developer programme and requires a partnership. But most of the benefit does not depend on it: opening client files, the knowledge base, client letters and translations all work with documents.
Is this a high-risk system under the AI Act?
As a rule, no. Searching documents, summarising and drafting does not fall into the high-risk categories. It is different as soon as a system sorts job applications or evaluates employees. Regardless of risk, the regulation requires AI literacy from every deployer, meaning training and documented rules of use.
What does it cost for a firm of twelve people?
Managed operation costs €15 per person per month, of which €8 is model credit in your organisation’s pool. If you self-host, the software costs nothing: it is MIT licensed. Everything else is on the pricing page.
Where is our data held, and do we need an IT department?
In the managed variant in European data centres with ISO 27001 certification, with self-hosting on your own server. You do not need an IT department. For self-hosting you need someone who can maintain a Linux server with Docker; Docker is the common technology for running server software in self-contained packages. The evidence is available in the Trust Center .

# AI and management software in Europe

AI and management software in Europe | EU Cowork AI

AI in everyday work
AI in property management: three workflows for when capacity runs short
In this sector it is not demand that is scarce, it is the capacity to process the work. This article walks through three workflows. You see how an AI colleague works with the resolutions, minutes and contracts of your properties. You also see what can genuinely be connected across Europe, and where the limits are.
Property
18 August 2026
Reading time: 13 minutes
- Starting point
- Enquiries answered from the resolution record
- Preparing the owners meeting
- Explaining statements and renovations
- Connectors and the route without an interface
- Data protection
- Frequently asked questions
In brief
- In Germany, 70% of property management firms report staff overload, 57% give up unprofitable mandates and almost 14% no longer take on any new clients at all. 1
- EU Cowork AI works with the documents of your properties: resolutions, minutes, house rules, maintenance and insurance contracts and past correspondence become the knowledge base, and you can put questions to it.
- The benefit starts before the interface. An interface is the technical route along which two programs exchange data. Management software in this sector is largely closed across Europe, but the documents are sitting there as files anyway.
- Legally binding declarations stay with the management office, and owner and tenant data stays in Europe or on your own server and does not train any models.
On this page
- Starting point
- Enquiries answered from the resolution record
- Preparing the owners meeting
- Explaining statements and renovations
- Connectors and the route without an interface
- Data protection
- Frequently asked questions
Starting point: the bottleneck is processing, not the market
The German association of property managers published its industry barometer in September 2025. 70% of property management firms report staff overload, a third of them severely. The reason: vacancies stay unfilled. The consequence appears in the same survey: 57% part with unprofitable mandates, 63% with time-consuming properties, and almost 14% no longer take on any new clients at all, rising above 20% among the smallest firms. 1 A market in which owner associations are left without a manager does not have a demand problem. It has a processing problem.
The rest of Europe knows the same work under different names. In France, the syndics of a single association alone manage some 4.5 million lots (as of 2023). 57% of its members work as administrateur de biens or as syndic de copropriete. 2 In Spain, administradores de fincas face a stock of 25.7 million dwellings. 42.7% of them were built before 1980, and the annual renovation rate is between 0.11 and 0.15%. 3 In Italy the management office is itself a micro business: 94.8% of all Italian enterprises have at most nine employees, and management offices typically sit below that. 10 At the same time, the condominium has for years received the invoices of its tradespeople and suppliers electronically through the Sistema di Interscambio (SdI), the state exchange system for electronic invoices. Assigning them to the individual owner associations is the management’s job. In Sweden, 100 public housing companies worked together in the digitalisation programme of the Allmännytta. They cover around 65% of the stock and more than a million tenants. 4 And in Norway, borettslag and sameier are a widespread form of management made almost entirely of documents: statutes, house rules, minutes of general meetings and board meetings, maintenance plans, correspondence with the shareholders.
Two things are the same everywhere. First, the work hangs on text: resolutions, minutes, house rules, maintenance and insurance contracts, tradespeople’s quotes, years of correspondence. Second, the small offices doing that work reach AI less easily than the large ones. In the EU, 19.9% of enterprises with ten or more employees use at least one AI technology. Among those with 10 to 49 employees it is 17.0%, and from 250 employees upwards 55.0%. 5 The gap between small and large is wider in every country than the gap between countries.
1
2
3
4
- Enquiries from the mailbox and the owner portal
- Knowledge base of resolutions, contracts and minutes
- Draft with its source reference
- Approval in the office, then sending and filing
How an enquiry moves through the management office: from the resolution record to the draft. Approval stays with the management.
Use case 1: answering enquiries from the resolution and contract record
An owner wants to replace her windows and asks whether she may and who pays. A tenant reports damp in the cellar storage and asks whether the repair has now been approved. A board member wants to know what the maintenance contract for the lift covers. Three enquiries, three times the same preparatory work: looking up what applies.
The AI colleague has those documents as a knowledge base: the declaration of division or the house regulations, the house rules, the collection of resolutions from recent years, maintenance and insurance contracts, past correspondence about the property. It produces a draft reply and names the source with it: the meeting, the date and the agenda item, including the wording. You read, trim and approve. The valuable part is not the finished text but the source reference underneath it.
1
2
3
- An enquiry from an owner, a tenant or the board
- The property’s resolutions, regulations and contracts, with permissions per tool
- A draft reply with its source, ready for review
The draft is built from the property’s own documents and shows what it rests on. Judging it happens in the office.
The line has to be drawn sharply. The assistant finds the passage and summarises it, it does not interpret it. Whether a declaration of division assigns the window front to individual ownership is the application of law, and if there is a dispute the specialist lawyer belongs at the table. No draft goes out without approval. Permissions apply down to individual tools: whoever may not see the files of another property does not see them through the AI either.
Use case 2: preparing the meeting from your own history of minutes
Eigentümerversammlung, assemblee generale, assemblea condominiale, junta de propietarios, generalforsamling: the meeting has a different name everywhere and means the same thing everywhere. Beforehand the agenda, the draft resolutions, the documents. Afterwards the minutes and the follow-up. In between a year in which nobody quite remembers what was deferred under item seven in the minutes before last.
The assistant reads the property’s series of minutes and compiles what is still open: deferred items, resolutions subject to conditions, works commissioned but not completed, recurring motions from the owners. Out of that comes a draft agenda, together with draft resolutions in the wording of comparable earlier ones. After the meeting, your notes become the first version of the minutes, in the structure your office uses anyway.
1
2
3
- Minutes of recent meetings, year by year
- One pass through a property’s history
- Draft agenda, open resolutions, first version of the minutes
The series of minutes produces three drafts for one meeting. Resolution texts are worded and owned by the management.
In Germany a change of format comes on top. Owners can resolve, with at least three quarters of the votes cast, to hold a purely virtual meeting for at most three years. If such a resolution is passed before 1 January 2028, a meeting in person must be held at least once a year up to and including 2028, unless this is waived unanimously. 6 So virtual meetings create more written preparation and follow-up, not less.
And this is where the sharpest limit in this article sits. A sloppily worded resolution can be challenged, and nothing about that changes if the first draft came out of a machine. The assistant supplies a template from your own records; it is worded, checked and owned by the management, and nothing is sent on its own.
Use case 3: explaining statements and renovations in the language of the owners
Every statement of costs produces follow-up questions, and those questions look much the same year after year. In Germany, the allocation of carbon dioxide costs along a tiered model has been added since 2023. On top of that comes a duty: where remotely readable equipment is installed, users have to be given monthly consumption information, compared with the previous month, the same month of the previous year and a standardised average user. 7 That is exactly the kind of calculation rule that has to be explained per property and per year: to the owners, to the tenants and to the board.
The assistant writes that explanation once from your own documents and then again and again: as an annex to the statement, as a reply to the follow-up question, as a section in the circular. The same pattern carries the second big topic. In Spain the ministry is aiming for 1.2 million renovated dwellings by 2030, while at the current pace around 285,000 can be expected. 3 A renovation resolution rarely fails for lack of will and often because nobody has put the funding conditions, the state of the building and the cost consequences side by side. That is precisely the compilation the assistant can prepare, provided the management has stored the funding conditions itself.
1
2
3
- The statement and cost allocation as they come out of the specialist software
- Explanatory building blocks and self-stored funding conditions
- The same explanation in the languages of the owners
Explained once, used many times. The calculation stays in the accounting software, and the original version remains authoritative.
Because owner associations on the Spanish coast and in French holiday regions are internationally mixed, the same explanation is produced in several languages on request. Two limits go with that. The calculation itself is done by the accounting software or the metering service; the AI explains the result, it does not recalculate it. And the legally authoritative version remains the original language, with the translation being a service that carries this note on the document. The assistant gives no assurance about eligibility for funding.
Connectors: the benefit starts before the interface
Now the uncomfortable truth: management software in this sector is largely closed across Europe. For the widely used German systems casavi, Immoware24, DOMUS and objego, no public developer documentation could be found in August 2026. The Spanish fincas programmes Gesfincas and NetFincas name neither an API nor a web service on their sites. Both are described routes along which another program could fetch data. For the French product group there is no verified finding, which is why it does not appear in a single row of this table.
That matters less than it sounds. The three workflows above do not depend on the specialist software. Resolutions, minutes, contracts and correspondence exist as files anyway, and the knowledge base needs no interface for them. The connection itself runs through MCP, an open standard for linking external systems. Where an AI connection of that kind is genuinely documented, it is listed here, checked in August 2026:
Software (country)

Connection via MCP possible: contacts, invoices, credit notes, dunning letters

Connection via MCP possible; for your own office a self-generated key is enough
If the software has no interface, the route runs via exports, and here that is no makeshift. Every management system hands out property and unit lists as a table, statements and dunning runs as PDF. Those outputs go into the knowledge base together with the document store. The difference from a real connection should be named honestly: you get no live status, but a status with a date on it. For the resolution record, contracts and history that is no loss, because those documents do not change by the hour. For open items and payment status it is one. There the route runs via the connected accounting system.
How a connection via MCP works in principle, and which systems are prepared, is described on the integrations page.
Data protection: owner and tenant data stays in Europe
A management office holds names, addresses, payment behaviour, arrears and occasionally details about accessibility needs. With data like that, the question of where it is stored is not theoretical. EU Cowork AI runs on your own server or managed in data centres with ISO 27001 certification. Model processing takes place in the EU, and customer data does not train any models. The data processing agreement and the subprocessor list are published openly on the website.
The advantage should not be made bigger than it is. If personal data is transferred to a recipient in a third country, that is, outside the European Economic Area, Chapter V of the General Data Protection Regulation applies. It calls for its own legal basis and an assessment of the legal situation in the destination country. If storage and processing stay within the European Economic Area, that assessment step falls away and what remains is ordinary processing on instructions under Article 28. European processing does not make the processing lawful automatically. It makes it easier to justify.
On top of that comes a point that is rarely spelled out. In Norway, 71.0% of the enterprises that use AI use commercial off-the-shelf software, in Sweden 62.1%. 5 Such tools are usable, but they do not know the business: not the resolutions, not the contracts, not the history of minutes. The difference lies not in the model, but in what it is allowed to reach and where it does its computing.
Finally, on the AI Act: an internal assistant that writes drafts and searches your own documents is as a rule minimal risk. This sector needs to pay attention elsewhere, because AI that decides on access to housing or assesses creditworthiness can fall into the high-risk category. EU Cowork AI supports the administrative work and does not select prospective tenants. This article is not legal advice.
Frequently asked questions from property management
Our management software has no interface. Is EU Cowork AI still useful for us?
Yes, and in this sector especially. Resolutions, minutes, house rules, contracts and correspondence exist as files, and that is exactly what the knowledge base is built from. Where figures from the specialist software are needed, the route runs via exports or via the connected accounting system.
Does the AI word our resolutions?
It supplies a template based on the wording of earlier resolutions for your property. The resolution text is worded, checked and owned by the management, because resolution texts have legal effect and a sloppily drafted wording can be challenged. A language model, the program behind the AI, can produce errors. That is why every text is a draft for review, not a verified statement.
How current is an answer from the knowledge base?
As current as the documents you have stored. Minutes that were never filed do not exist for the assistant, and outdated house regulations produce an outdated answer. Maintaining the knowledge base is work and belongs in the plan. Because every answer names its source, you can see in seconds which version it rests on.
We manage properties in several countries and languages. Does that work?
Yes. The knowledge base can hold documents in several languages, and the answer comes back in the language you ask in. For notices, invitations and explanatory letters that is the everyday benefit. The legally authoritative version remains the original language, and the translation carries that note.
Does an assistant like this fall under the AI Act?
An internal assistant that writes drafts and searches your own documents is as a rule minimal risk and triggers no approval or registration obligations. As a deployer you make sure your staff have sufficient AI literacy. Caution is required where AI decides about people, for instance when selecting prospective tenants or assessing creditworthiness. This answer is not legal advice.
Where is our owner and tenant data held?
With self-hosting on your own server, in the managed variant in data centres with ISO 27001 certification. Model requests are processed in the EU, and customer data does not train any models. The evidence is available in the Trust Center .
What does it cost for an office of eight people?
Managed operation costs €15 per person per month, of which €8 is model credit in your organisation’s shared pool. If you self-host, the software costs nothing: it is MIT licensed. All details are on the pricing page.
See it on a property of your own
Bring a set of minutes, a collection of resolutions or a statement of costs, and we will walk through the workflow together. Or sign up and be among the first to start.

AI in everyday work
AI in practices and pharmacies: three workflows that give care time back
A report for the payer, a hygiene plan, patient information in four languages: in practices and pharmacies from Kiel to Málaga, paperwork eats the time meant for people. Three workflows show what an AI colleague takes on and what it explicitly does not do here.
Practice and pharmacy
18 August 2026
Reading time: 10 minutes
- Starting point
- Where the line runs
- Reports and applications
- The team knowledge base
- Information in several languages
- Connectors to industry software
- Data protection
- Frequently asked questions
In brief
- In Germany, 91% of doctors in private practice feel overloaded by administrative tasks, and around 61 days a year go into bureaucracy. 1
- Every pharmacy in Germany spends more than 20 hours a week managing supply shortages. 10
- EU Cowork AI works with your own documents. Templates, quality manual, hygiene and emergency plans and your country’s billing rules become a knowledge base you can query in your own words. Every answer names its source.
- No diagnosis, no triage, no medication check, no substitution suggestion. That line is not caution, it is product law.
On this page
- Starting point
- Where the line runs
- Reports and applications
- The team knowledge base
- Information in several languages
- Connectors to industry software
- Data protection
- Frequently asked questions
Starting point: paperwork eats the time meant for care
The finding is the same everywhere, only the figures carry different names. In Germany, 91% of doctors in private practice feel administratively overloaded, around 61 days a year go into bureaucracy, and more than 5,000 GP positions are unfilled. 1 In France, according to a 2019 survey, general practitioners work 54 hours a week on average, 5.5 of them on administration and coordination. 4
In the pharmacy it is no better. Every German pharmacy spends more than 20 hours a week managing supply shortages. 10 In Norway, only 13% of pharmacy managers handle administrative work within regular working hours. 7 In Spain the network counts 22,273 community pharmacies, 86.9% of them individually owned and 64.5% outside the provincial capitals. 6
A single crisis story would still be wrong. In Germany the number of pharmacy premises fell by 440 to 16,601 in 2025. 2 In Austria it has risen since 2016 and stood at 1,445 public pharmacies at the end of 2025. 3 In France, 260 pharmacies closed in 2024. 5 What these markets share is not the crisis, but the writing load on ever fewer shoulders.
Where the line runs
In this field the line belongs at the beginning. EU Cowork AI makes no diagnosis and no tentative diagnosis, does no triage, no urgency rating and no appointment scheduling by symptom. It gives no treatment recommendation, no dosage statement, no interaction or medication check, no substitution and no generic-swap suggestion, and it evaluates no findings, images or lab values.
The reason is product law, not caution. As soon as a system contributes to a diagnosis or a treatment decision, it is a medical device. That makes it high-risk AI under Annex I of the AI Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689. Since the amendment by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 that category applies from 2 August 2028. Pharmaceutical substitution remains a decision for the pharmacist, based on verified databases, and the diagnosis remains a decision for the doctor. And nothing leaves the practice or the pharmacy without human approval.
Use case 1: reports and applications from your own practice knowledge
The payer asks for a statement, the insurer requests a progress report, an authority sends a questionnaire. The AI colleague knows your templates, the earlier letters to the same office and your team’s wording blocks. It gathers what your documents already say and files a draft in your usual tone for review.
In the pharmacy the same workflow carries the clawback appeal: summarise the facts, name the evidence, structure the objection. In Norway, writing certificates is a block of work of its own; in France, certificates and coordination fill those 5.5 admin hours a week. 4 Repetitive, text-heavy, rule-bound: exactly where a draft from your own documents pays off.
1
2
3
- The payer’s request
- Templates, earlier letters, wording blocks
- A draft in your usual tone, waiting for a signature
The draft is built from your documents. The content stays the practice’s responsibility.
What deliberately does not happen: no medical assessment, no estimate of an appeal’s chances, no automatic sending. A language model can produce errors; every text is a draft for review.
Use case 2: the team’s knowledge becomes queryable
What is the reprocessing procedure for this instrument? Which cover arrangement applies during the summer holidays? Today such questions interrupt the management. Your quality manual, hygiene and emergency plans, work instructions, device documentation and your country’s billing rules become a knowledge base. The AI colleague answers from it and names the source, checkable in seconds.
The benefit is greatest where knowledge sits with single people. In Spain, 86.9% of pharmacies are individually owned. 6 If the owner is away, half the operating knowledge is away too. New pharmacy technicians and stand-ins ask in their own language and get answers from the same documents. Whoever may not see the personnel folder does not see it through the AI either.
1
2
3
- Quality manual, hygiene plan and billing rules
- Access governed per tool, every call logged
- An answer with its source, checkable in seconds
The knowledge base answers from your documents and shows where each answer comes from.
The flip side belongs in the picture: an outdated filing system produces outdated answers. For guidelines and standards, the licence decides whether they may go in.
Use case 3: information in several languages
A product is unavailable, the practice closes for two weeks, the prescription process is switched over. From one version come the notice on the door, the short briefing for the counter and the message to patients, each in the languages of your catchment area. In a rural pharmacy with two staff, that is the difference between a notice and none.
The line is especially sharp here, because the text reaches people. Every version is approved by the team first. Package leaflets, consent forms and anything legally binding remain authoritative in their official version; the translation is an aid to understanding.
1
2
3
- One version, written by your own team
- Language versions from the same source text
- Professional approval by the team
One piece of information becomes several language versions. The official version stays authoritative.
If you open a chat for patients, you must disclose that a machine is answering; even then it must not rate symptoms.
Connectors: what can really be linked
An AI colleague is only as useful as what it is allowed to reach. A connector is the link to another program. MCP is an open standard for such links. Through it, programs can be addressed that have a documented interface, meaning an official route for exchanging data. Each tool has its own permission, and every call is logged. For practices and pharmacies the field is closed. The verified state of play for AI connections in August 2026:
Software (country)
Interface
Connection to EU Cowork AI
Kaddio (SE)
GraphQL API, publicly documented; access with an account and the add-on
Connection via MCP possible, the only verified case in the sector
Dentalink (ES)
REST API documented; administrators create the access
Connection via MCP possible, through the practice administrator
CGM PROFIM and Wingesfar (IT)
No public API, only the vendor’s own add-on modules
No connector, the route runs via exports and documents
Sistema Tessera Sanitaria (IT)
Specifications public, access via credentials and a PIN
An authority channel. Preparing yes, sending no
medatixx, IXOS and awinta (DE)
No public developer portal
Only through the vendor’s partner channel
Telematics infrastructure, ePA and e-prescription (DE)
gematik specifications are open, access only through approved components
No connector, and we are not holding one out either

Connection via MCP possible: invoices, receipts, contacts
Microsoft 365 (EU-wide)

MCP server available from Microsoft; email, calendar and files
France, Austria and Liechtenstein are missing on purpose, and so are CGM MEDISTAR, TURBOMED and WINAPO: we have no verified finding on them, and a promise that breaks in the first conversation costs more than it brings. More under integrations .
The benefit here does not hang on the connector anyway. Reports, applications, notices and quality documents are documents, and documents need no system connection. Anyone waiting for their practice management system to be connected is waiting for the wrong thing.
Data protection: health data
Health data are special categories of personal data under Article 9 GDPR. Above them sits a professional secrecy duty backed by criminal law in every country: in France the secret professionnel under Article 226-13 of the Code pénal, in Italy the segreto professionale, in Spain the secreto profesional, in Germany medical and pharmaceutical confidentiality. A data processing agreement does not lift that. This article is not legal advice.
EU Cowork AI runs on your own server or, in the managed variant, in ISO 27001 certified data centres. The certification sits with the data centre operator, not with us. Requests to the language models are processed in the EU, and customer data does not train any models. What we do not say: that your data never leaves your business. In the managed variant it does, under control and within Europe. Anyone who does not want that for health data operates the platform themselves. The data processing agreement and the subprocessor list are public.
In France there is one particularity. Anyone hosting health data for third parties needs HDS certification, the French approval for hosting health data, under Article L1111-8 of the Code de la santé publique. 8 Institutions that operate their own information system themselves are exempt. Plainly: self-hosting is the shorter route, because then nobody is hosting for third parties. For the managed variant we settle the HDS question with you.
That leaves the objection that you already have an AI tool. Usually it is off-the-shelf software: in Norway, 71% of AI-using companies deploy ready-made software, in Sweden 62%. 9 A tool like that does not know your quality manual. That is the gap a knowledge base from your own documents closes.
Frequently asked questions from practices and pharmacies
Can the AI help with diagnosis, triage or medication?
No. EU Cowork AI makes no diagnosis, does no triage, gives no treatment or dosage statement, checks no interactions and suggests no substitution or generic swap. As soon as a system contributes to a treatment decision, it is a medical device and high-risk AI under Annex I of the AI Act, a different product with different obligations.
Can you connect EU Cowork AI to our practice management system, such as medatixx or IXOS, or to the electronic health record?
The systems in our markets mostly have no publicly documented interface. Where one exists, the route runs through the vendor. We do not connect to the German telematics infrastructure with the electronic health record and e-prescription: the gematik specifications are open, but access runs only through approved components. Anyone promising you a connection there is promising too much.
Does our use fall under the AI Act?
Two things apply to you as a deployer: the AI literacy duty since 2 February 2025 and the transparency duty since 2 August 2026, when people interact with an AI system. An internal assistant for writing and looking things up is not a high-risk system. It becomes high-risk where decisions are made about people, for instance when pre-sorting job applications. This answer is not legal advice.
We are in France. What does HDS certification mean for us?
Anyone hosting health data for third parties needs HDS certification in France, under Article L1111-8 of the Code de la santé publique. If you operate EU Cowork AI yourself, the exemption for institutions that run their own information system applies. No hosting for third parties arises. For the managed variant we settle the HDS question beforehand.
May patient data go into the knowledge base at all?
For the benefits this article describes, it does not need to: quality manual, hygiene and emergency plans, work instructions, templates and billing rules contain no patient data. Where health data is processed after all, Article 9 GDPR, professional secrecy and the access rights in the system apply. You settle the legal basis before the first file.
What does it cost for a team of ten?
Managed operation costs €15 per person per month, of which €8 is model credit in your organisation’s pool. If you self-host, the software costs nothing: it is MIT licensed. All details on the pricing page.

Bring a letter to a payer or a hygiene plan, and we will walk through the workflow together. Or sign up and be among the first to start.

AI in everyday work
AI in trades and SMEs: three workflows that give office time back
Quotes, work reports, looking up regulations: Swiss businesses lose their evenings in the office, not on the job site. This article walks through three workflows. You see how an AI colleague works with your company’s knowledge, what can connect to your software, and where the limits are.
Trades and SMEs
10 February 2026
Reading time: 9 minutes
- Starting point
- Quotes and correspondence
- From site notes to a clean report
- The company knowledge base
- Connectors to industry software
- Data protection
- Frequently asked questions
In brief
- Translation (52%) and correspondence (47%) are the most common AI applications in Swiss SMEs, exactly the work that piles up in the evening. 3
- EU Cowork AI works with your company’s knowledge: quote templates, utility regulations, work instructions and past reports become a knowledge base you can query.
- Your data stays in Switzerland or on your own server and does not train any models.
- Software with an open interface can be connected, for example Microsoft 365, bexio or KLARA. An interface is the point where two programs exchange data. The route for this is called the Model Context Protocol (MCP): with permissions per tool and a log entry for every access.
On this page
- Starting point
- Quotes and correspondence
- From site notes to a clean report
- The company knowledge base
- Connectors to industry software
- Data protection
- Frequently asked questions
Starting point: administration grows faster than the business
More than 60% of Swiss companies perceive their administrative burden as high. Building regulations weigh heaviest, at 59%. 1 Counted across the whole country, avoidable bureaucracy adds up to around 30 billion francs per year, according to a study by ifo and BSS. 2
In the trades the direction is clear: in a German association survey of 10,630 businesses, 74% report that bureaucratic effort has grown over the past five years. 4 In the electrical trade there is deadline pressure on top. The grid operator asks the property owner in writing to submit the safety verification report (SiNa), at least six months before the inspection period expires. If the report is still missing after two reminders, enforcement passes to ESTI. 5 The deadline pressure lands on the business that repairs the installation and delivers the paperwork.
At the same time, AI has arrived in SMEs: within one year, the share of Swiss SMEs using AI rose from 22 to 34%, most often for translation and correspondence. 3 So the question is no longer whether a business uses AI. The question is whether it works with the company’s knowledge, and where the data ends up.
1
2
3
4
- Keywords from the job site, typed or dictated
- Draft built from templates and company knowledge
- Review and approval in the business
- Sending and filing, fully logged
How a work report moves through the business: from the notes on the way home to the filed document. Approval stays with a person.
Use case 1: quotes and correspondence from your own company knowledge
An enquiry arrives in the morning by email: bathroom renovation, three keywords, two photos. The AI colleague knows the company’s quote templates, price lists and past quotes. It suggests line items, writes the cover text in the company’s tone and files the draft for review. You remove one item, adjust one price and send the quote.
The same applies to the correspondence around it: rescheduling, payment reminders, replying to a complaint, a translation for a French-speaking client. The draft is built from the previous correspondence and your own documents; approval stays with a person.
1
2
3
- The customer’s enquiry, as brief as it arrives
- The company’s templates, price lists and past quotes
- A quote draft in the company’s tone, ready for review
The draft is built from company knowledge, not from the model’s memory. Line items and prices are decided by the business.
The difference to a chat in the browser: the draft is based on your documents rather than on pasted-in snippets. And your quote and costing stay in your own instance instead of in someone else’s chat account. An instance is your own copy of the system, kept separate from other customers.
Use case 2: from site notes to a clean report
On the way home the technician types or dictates three sentences into the phone; the device’s dictation function is enough. He notes what was done, what was used and what stood out. Out of that come the time-and-materials report in the company format, the materials list and a defect description for the site management: worded, numbered, ready to file. A quantities summary for the site measurements is drafted too. The checking stays with the business.
In the electrical trade, clean paperwork is about more than tidiness: measurement and test protocols and the safety verification report follow fixed forms. 6 Filling in and checking them remains the job of the authorised inspector. The AI colleague takes over the writing around them, from the cover letter to the grid operator to the defect list for the customer.
1
2
3
- Three short sentences from the drive home
- One input, three documents in the company format
- Report, materials list and defect description, ready for approval
Three sentences become three documents ready to file. Nothing goes out without approval.
What deliberately does not happen: no document is sent automatically. Every report waits for approval, and every change remains traceable.
Use case 3: the company’s knowledge becomes queryable
Which utility regulation applies to the metering installation with this grid operator? How did we service this installation two years ago? Today, questions like these interrupt the management. A knowledge base is a collection of your own documents that the AI colleague is allowed to search: work instructions, utility regulations, manufacturer documents and past reports. From those it answers such questions and names the source. That way the answer can be checked in seconds.
New employees ask in their own language and get answers from the same documents. The safety briefing in Portuguese is generated from the company’s German fact sheet. Important for standards: texts such as the Swiss low-voltage installation standard (NIN) are copyrighted. Whether they may go into a knowledge base depends on your Electrosuisse licence. Clarify the scope before uploading. Your own documents belong there anyway.
1
2
3
- A question in everyday language, on the phone or in the office
- Your own documents, with permissions per tool and a full log
- An answer with its source, checkable in seconds
The knowledge base answers from the company’s documents and shows where each answer comes from.
Permissions apply down to individual tools: whoever may not see the payroll folder does not see it through the AI either. Every access is recorded in the audit log, the running record of who retrieved what and when.
Connectors: what can be linked to your software
An AI colleague is only as useful as what it is allowed to reach. A connector is the ready-made link between EU Cowork AI and another program. It becomes possible when that program has a documented API, that is, an interface through which programs exchange data. The framework for this is MCP, an open standard for connecting external systems. Permissions apply per individual tool, and every call is logged. This is the state of play for common trades and SME software, checked in August 2026, from the AI connection to bexio and KLARA through to Microsoft 365:
Software
Interface

Is your software missing from the list? Much of the daily work runs without any system connection at all, from quotes to the knowledge base. How a connection via MCP works in principle, and which systems are prepared, is described on the integrations page.
Data protection: your costing stays in the business
Quotes, costings and customer files are trade secrets. Under the revised Swiss Data Protection Act, the business remains responsible for personal data even when an AI tool processes it. If a provider processes that data for you, a data processing agreement is required. That is the contract setting out what the provider may do with the data. This article is not legal advice.
EU Cowork AI is operated in Switzerland or runs on your own server. Customer data does not train any models. Requests to the language model are processed in the EU. The data processing agreement and the subprocessor list are published openly on the website.
In practice this means: the price list you calculate with ends up in nobody’s training data, and when a customer asks where the data is held, you answer in one sentence.
Frequently asked questions from trades and SMEs
My industry software has no interface, for example SORBA or ElektroForm. Is EU Cowork AI still useful for me?
Yes. Quotes, reports, correspondence and the knowledge base work with documents and need no system connection. Where a connection is missing, the route runs via exports, via the SIA 451 exchange format for bills of quantities, or via the connected accounting software.
Does the AI write my quote on its own?
No, it writes the draft from your templates and price lists. Line items, prices and the approval stay with you. A language model can produce errors. That is why every text is a draft for review, not a verified statement.
May I load the NIN standards into the knowledge base?
Standard texts such as the NIN are copyrighted. Whether you may load them into the knowledge base depends on your licence from Electrosuisse. Clarify this before uploading. Your own work instructions, the grid operators’ utility regulations, manufacturer documents and your reports make up the larger part of your company knowledge, and they are yours anyway. This answer is not legal advice.
What does it cost for a ten-person business?
Managed operation costs €15 per person per month, in Switzerland CHF 14. Of that, €8 or CHF 7.50 is model credit that everyone in your organisation shares. If you self-host, the software costs nothing: it is MIT licensed. All details are on the pricing page.
Where is our data held?
In the managed variant in Switzerland, with self-hosting on your own server. Customer data does not train any models, and requests to the language model are processed in the EU. The evidence is available in the Trust Center .
Do we need an IT department for this?
No. In the managed variant the operator takes care of operation, updates and backups. You manage users and permissions in the admin panel, your organisation’s administration screen. For self-hosting you need someone who can maintain a Linux server with Docker, which can also be an IT service provider.
Does it work on the phone, on site?
Yes. EU Cowork AI runs as a PWA on iPhone, Android devices and the desktop. A PWA is a web application that can be installed on the device like an app. Taking notes, photographing and looking things up works where the work happens; your device’s dictation function is enough. The finished report waits in the office for approval.

# AI in manufacturing: ERP, Abacus, SAP

URL: https://eucowork.ai/en/blog/ki-produktion

AI in everyday work
AI in manufacturing: three workflows that keep knowledge in the company
Your most experienced employee retires in two years, the specification for the next quote runs to 140 pages, and the audit is due in spring. This article walks through three workflows to show how an AI colleague works with your company’s knowledge, what can be connected to your ERP, and where the limits are.
Manufacturing
17 March 2026
Reading time: 12 minutes
- Starting point
- Preserving practical knowledge
- Specifications and tenders
- Quality assurance and audits
- Connectors to ERP and office software
- Trade secrets and data protection
- Frequently asked questions
In brief
- Only 17% of SMEs have a defined digital strategy, compared with almost 50% of large companies. 1
- In the Swiss tech industry, AI close to production is mostly still at the trial stage: half of the companies have not considered it, 10% are running pilots. 2
- EU Cowork AI works with your company’s knowledge. Service reports, test protocols, notes on bills of materials and change requests become a knowledge base: a collection of your own documents that you can question in plain sentences.
- Your design data stays in Switzerland or on your own server and does not train any models. Your ERP can be connected if it has a documented interface. An interface is the point where two programs exchange data; the Model Context Protocol (MCP) is the open standard an AI program uses to reach it.
On this page
- Starting point
- Preserving practical knowledge
- Specifications and tenders
- Quality assurance and audits
- Connectors to ERP and office software
- Trade secrets and data protection
- Frequently asked questions
Starting point: the strategy is missing, the knowledge is retiring
Only 17% of SMEs have a defined digital strategy, compared with almost 50% of large companies. That comes from a Swissmem survey on Industry 4.0 with 267 companies from German-speaking Switzerland and 54 from the French-speaking part. 1 With artificial intelligence the gap between announcement and shop floor is wider still. ETH Zurich, together with Swissmem and Next Industries, surveyed more than 200 Swiss tech companies. Half have not even considered AI close to production, and 10% are running pilots. 2
There are good reasons for the hesitation. Swissmem names security risks and data protection questions, regulatory requirements, and data structure and data quality as the hurdles. 4 Putting design data into somebody else’s cloud buys you a problem that no efficiency gain makes up for. And anyone with an archive that grew over thirty years knows that data quality does not appear at the push of a button. The workable answer is not to wait, but to start small and under control.
Because a clock is running, and it hangs in the HR office. Swissmem names the loss of knowledge through retirements as a core problem. The association runs the research project Digitaler Wissenserhalt im Unternehmen, in which language models make decades of inconsistent documentation findable again. 3 A language model is a program that reads text and writes text of its own. So the industry association is working on exactly the case your workshop lives through every week: the answer is in a document nobody can find any more, and the colleague who knows it by heart has two years left before retirement.
In food production there is a legal track on top. Self-monitoring according to the HACCP principles is an obligation of the business. 5 Industry guides to good practice are reviewed by the Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office. The basis for this is Article 80 of the Swiss Foodstuffs and Utility Articles Ordinance. 6 The obligation stays with the business. The paperwork around it does not have to.
1
2
3
4
- Service reports, test protocols and change requests from decades of work
- A knowledge base inside your own company, with permissions per tool
- A question in everyday language, from the shop floor or the office
- An answer with its source document, checked by the specialist
How company knowledge comes back to the workplace: from the archive that grew over decades to an answer with its source. The judgement stays with a person.
Use case 1: practical knowledge stays in the company
A machine built in 2011 has stopped at the customer’s site. The service technician is looking for the cause and is certain the same fault has occurred before, except that it is written up in a service report nobody can find. Two doors down, the design engineer asks why a variant was built with that particular bearing arrangement back then. The same employee can answer both questions, and he retires in two years.
Service reports, test protocols, notes on bills of materials and change requests go into the knowledge base exactly as they are: as PDFs, as scans, as a folder structure that grew over time. Questions are asked in everyday language, the way you would ask a colleague, and not with search commands: which fault has already occurred on which series, why that bearing arrangement was chosen, what the acceptance protocol said. The answer comes with a reference to the document it is based on. So you look it up in seconds instead of having to take it on trust.
1
2
3
- A question in everyday language, from service or engineering
- Reports, protocols and change requests, with permissions per tool
- An answer with its source document, checkable in seconds
The knowledge base answers from the company’s own documents and shows where each answer comes from. What sits in the archive becomes a working tool again.
Permissions apply down to individual tools: whoever may not see the costing does not see it through the AI either. Every access is recorded in the audit log, a record of who opened which document and when. Start with one machine type or one series and check the first answers against cases you know by heart. The quality of the answers grows with the quality of the archive, and the business sees on its own example what orderly filing is worth from now on.
Use case 2: examining the specification before the quote
The customer’s requirements specification arrives with 140 pages. The submission deadline is in ten days, and the only person who can read it is the senior engineer who is fully booked anyway. The document goes into the AI colleague, and out comes a structured requirements list: what is required, which chapter it appears in, which standard is cited and which tolerance is named.
In a second step that list is matched against your own specifications, standards lists and earlier bids from the knowledge base. What your portfolio covers is shown as covered, with a reference to your own specification. What it does not cover is flagged. What is worded ambiguously goes onto the list of questions for the customer, with the exact spot in the specification. The senior engineer then reads the flagged passages instead of all 140 pages, and the decision whether to bid rests on a basis rather than on a feeling.
1
2
3
- Customer specification, exactly as it arrives
- Your own specifications, standards lists and earlier bids
- Requirements list with flagged gaps and open questions
The comparison is built from your portfolio, not from the model’s memory. Whether to bid is decided by the business.
What deliberately does not happen: the AI colleague makes no commitment and replaces no technical clarification. It delivers a draft with sources, and a language model can miss a requirement or classify it wrongly. That is why the list belongs in the hands of the specialists who judge what is feasible. The gain is that the review starts on day one instead of day seven.
Use case 3: quality assurance and audits in food production
The IFS Food or BRCGS audit is due in March. The question catalogue is mirrored against your own HACCP and quality management manual, and out comes a gap list: which question the manual answers, where there is only a cross-reference, where there is nothing. Quality assurance works through that list instead of reading the manual from the start three times over.
The second pile is supplier documentation: specifications, certificates, certificates of analysis. The AI colleague summarises them, flags expiry dates and names what is missing. The third case is multilingual label and declaration drafts as well as operating instructions. They are produced with your company glossary, that is with your own list of agreed terms, and use the same terms across every language. The order of ingredients and the highlighting of allergens are check points on the quality assurance list, not results produced by the machine.
1
2
3
- Audit questions, supplier documents and recipe files
- Comparison against your own HACCP and quality manual
- Gap list, document overview and label draft for approval
One input becomes three drafts. None of them replaces sign-off by quality assurance.
The boundary here is drawn sharply, and rightly so. Self-monitoring is a statutory obligation of the business. 5 The AI colleague writes drafts and finds gaps; sign-off has to come from quality assurance. With labels and operating instructions, product liability is added on top: professional approval belongs explicitly to a person, and no text written by a machine is legally sound in itself. This article is not legal advice.
Connectors: what can be linked to your systems
An AI colleague is only as useful as what it is allowed to reach. MCP is an open standard that lets an AI program address another program. What it needs is a documented interface, that is a published connection point where two programs exchange data. Every single tool is released separately, and every call is logged. According to an analysis by Profondia, the most widely used ERP in Switzerland is Abacus with 17%, ahead of SAP with 16% and Microsoft Dynamics with 8%. 7 The table shows how far the AI connection to common software in manufacturing and food production reaches today, checked in August 2026. The middle column gives the technical names of those interfaces; the column that matters for you is the right one.
Software
